jobs.title: Senior Product Operations Manager, Evaluation Quality
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We’re looking for a senior operator to own the quality bar behind Harvey’s human evaluations. As we scale globally, the volume of eval work is growing 10x, but volume only matters if the output is trusted. This role makes Human Data’s signal decision-grade: rigorous, calibrated, and reproducible enough that Product, Engineering, and AI Research act on it to ship.

As a member of our Evaluation Operations team, you’ll work alongside our Evaluation Operations Manager (who runs throughput and coordination) and partner closely with Applied Legal Researchers, Product, Engineering, and AI Research. You'll set the standard for what "good" looks like across eval data and methodology, and own the data analyses to make conclusions that teams will rely on, building the stakeholder trust that lets EPD act on the signal.

What You'll Do

  • Own the quality bar for Harvey’s human evaluations: define what “good” looks like for eval methodology and data analysis, and produce decision-grade outputs for EPD

  • Author and maintain the evaluation guidelines, instructions, and databases that contract attorneys work from

  • Standardize and streamline rubric and evaluation design into repeatable templates and one documented methodology, partnering with Applied Legal Research (ALR), who supplies feature-specific legal depth

  • Own contract-attorney quality: onboarding, calibration training, inter-rater reliability, and the feedback loop (including benchmarks and gold references) that keeps judgment consistent across attorneys and over time

  • Conducting quantitative and qualitative statistical analyses, diagnosing error states, investigating root causes, and turning raw eval results into a structured, prioritized signal Product and ALR can act on

  • Run QA on vendor and contract-attorney deliverables against a defined bar before results inform a launch decision

  • Ensure the quality bar holds across jurisdictions and non-English geographies as coverage expands

  • Establish one standard, documented way to analyze eval results, and build lightweight operational dashboards to track rater capability and eval-program health

  • Support ALR in a review step that certifies an evaluation is sound before it scales to contract attorneys

  • Partner with ALR and Analytics to determine where human eval aligns with online signal and where it can provide expanded insights

What You Have

  • 6+ years in product operations, research operations, evaluation/QA operations, or quality program management

  • A track record of owning quality inputs (guidelines, instructions, benchmarks, QA procedures) for complex, expert-driven or human-in-the-loop work

  • Experience onboarding, training, and calibrating a distributed pool of expert raters, annotators, or reviewers, and running the feedback loop that improves their quality over time

  • Enough grounding in measurement concepts (calibration, inter-rater reliability, sampling, rubric design) to independently set up and own the quality of our evaluation loop yourself

  • Experience with running quantitative and qualitative data analyses, interpreting and running statistical tests on evaluation data (natively or with AI tool support), and communicating conclusions to various stakeholders

  • A record of scaling and streamlining evaluation quality processes under shipping pressure, with a bias toward documentation and reproducibility over one-off analysis

  • Ability to work deeply with domain experts (e.g., ALR / lawyers) and translate nuanced judgment into repeatable, documented standards

  • Strong cross-functional coordination across Product, Engineering, Research, ALR, and data providers/vendors

  • Clear communicator who can build credibility and trust with stakeholders

  • Bias to action and high ownership, from writing the guideline to auditing a vendor batch line by line

Bonus Points

  • Experience in legal tech or working with domain experts in regulated industries

  • Experience owning quality across multiple markets, languages, or jurisdictions

  • Built calibration, inter-rater reliability, or capability-tracking systems for annotation or evaluation pipelines

  • Experience transitioning evaluation work in-house or otherwise improving evaluation ROI

  • Familiarity with LLM-as-judge / automated evaluation used alongside human eval

  • Early employee at a hyper-growth startup, or experience at a world-class product or platform operations org

Compensation

$155,400 - $233,200 USD

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We’re hiring an experienced, hands-on leader for the GTM Strategy & Operations team within the Revenue Operations organization. This team serves as the core strategic and business partner function to the GTM organization, playing a critical role in driving GTM growth and operational excellence. In this role, you will lead a team of AMER Sales Business Partners and serve as a trusted advisor to AMER Sales Leadership.

What You'll Do

  • Partner with AMER Enterprise Sales Leadership on sales planning, including annual, half year, and quarterly GTM planning cycles. This will include leading AMER territory planning, headcount planning, and quota planning to help the organization achieve aggressive growth targets.

  • Partner with AMER Enterprise Sales Leadership to develop field strategy for the Americas and ensure alignment with the global operating model. This includes driving forecast rigor, pipeline generation strategies, CRM hygiene, data accuracy, and operating discipline to enable predictable growth.

  • Drive operating rigor and scalability by establishing and evolving the operating rhythms, processes, and cadences that enable disciplined execution and support sustained GTM growth.

  • Partner with GTM Enablement to identify capability gaps, develop targeted training programs, and support the onboarding and ramp of new AEs and SDRs.

  • Lead and develop a high performing team of AMER Sales Business Partners; continuously raise the bar on team capabilities, talent development, and operational excellence.

  • Lead high priority GTM initiatives that address complex, high-impact problems

What You Have

  • 10+ years in Revenue Operations or Sales Strategy & Operations, or a closely related field. Ideal candidates will have a combination of operational experience in GTM Strategy & Operations experience in a high-tech growth environment, and experience in investment banking, private equity, venture capital, strategy / management consulting, or other highly analytical roles.

  • 3+ years of people management experience required. A nice to have would be prior experience managing managers as well.

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills; you're energized by working across teams and can bring people together around shared goals

  • Demonstrated ability to be an effective business partner and lead a team of business partners, with the ability to build trusted relationships, navigate diverse working styles, and influence cross-functional stakeholders without direct authority.

Compensation

$212,000-$290,000 USD

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

Role Overview

The Staff Web Designer joins Harvey's Web team to define and elevate the design experience across harvey.ai and all web-facing surfaces. The team is responsible for translating Harvey's brand and product story into compelling, accessible, and high-performing web experiences that drive awareness, engagement, and pipeline. In this role, you will own and evolve the website design system, lead user research and testing initiatives, and set the quality bar for every page that ships. You will partner closely with web engineers, motion designers, product marketing, and brand stakeholders to deliver end-to-end design solutions at the pace a category-defining legal AI company demands. It is a rare opportunity to shape how the world first encounters Harvey—and to build the design infrastructure that scales that experience.

What You'll Do

  • Own and evolve the website design system—establishing scalable patterns, component libraries, and governance standards that maintain consistency and accelerate delivery across all web surfaces.

  • Lead the end-to-end design process for web projects, from concept and user research through interaction design, prototyping, and detailed technical specification hand-off to web engineers and motion designers.

  • Drive innovation through exploration, prototyping, and user testing to continuously improve user experience, conversion, and accessibility across harvey.ai and related properties.

  • Mentor junior web designers, embedding best practices around responsive design, accessibility, and design-system governance to raise the team's collective quality bar.

  • Run design demos, present work to marketing leadership and cross-functional stakeholders, and articulate design rationale with clarity and expertise.

  • Leverage AI tools and emerging technologies to accelerate design workflows, explore new interaction paradigms, and push the boundary of what a best-in-class legal AI website can be.

What You Have

  • 8+ years of professional design experience with a significant focus on web and digital product design, including demonstrated impact at a staff or senior-staff level.

  • A portfolio that showcases mastery of user experience design, interaction design, responsive web design, and design-system architecture.

  • Deep expertise in systems thinking—building, scaling, and governing design systems that serve multiple teams and use cases.

  • Strong command of modern design tools (e.g., Figma) and comfort working at the intersection of design and front-end development, including providing pixel-level specifications and technical hand-offs.

  • Demonstrated ability to leverage AI-assisted design workflows and a track record of raising quality and velocity in fast-paced, high-growth environments.

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, with experience running design reviews, stakeholder demos, and cross-functional critiques.

Compensation

$146,600 - $219,800 USD

Role Overview

The communications team builds and protects Harvey’s reputation. In this role you will lead tech and product communications for Harvey, shaping how two audiences understand our business: the AI community that wants to know how we build, and the lawyers who want to know what we deliver. You will partner closely with executive leadership, eng, product, and go-to-market. Reports to the Global Head of Communications.

 

What You'll Do

  • Own Harvey's product narrative: the story of what we build, how we build it, and why it matters for legal teams and society.

  • Turn complex engineering and product work into compelling stories for both technical and legal audiences.

  • Cultivate and deepen relationships with top-tier journalists, newsletter writers, podcasters, and influencers shaping how people talk about AI.

  • Reach our target audiences where they are: generate high-impact coverage across business, tech, and legal press, as well as creative placements beyond traditional media.

  • Elevate the external profiles of Harvey's executives, product leaders, and researchers through media training, press strategy, thought leadership, and speaking.

  • Build AI tools and workflows for yourself and the team.

 

What You Have

  • Fluency in AI. You use AI tools to do your own work better and make everyone more efficient.

  • 8+ years in product communications at a high-growth technology company or at a PR agency supporting engineering and product clients.

  • A track record of earned media across top-tier publications, podcasts, newsletters, and new media, and deep relationships with the people behind them.

  • A creative approach to reaching audiences, and a willingness to test new channels.

  • Experience supporting senior leaders and building executive visibility programs.

  • Clear, concise, human writing that makes complex technical work easy to understand.

  • Comfort moving quickly in a very fast-paced environment, and a collaborative approach to working with others.

 

Compensation

$177,000 - $260,000 USD

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Engineering
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey is building the infrastructure foundation behind one of the most ambitious AI product companies in the world. Our Core Infrastructure team powers every user interaction across Harvey’s legal AI platform, which already processes billions of prompt tokens and millions of daily requests for leading law firms, enterprises, and other high-stakes customers.

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead Core Infrastructure from Bengaluru as we scale the platform, the team, and the next generation of Harvey products. This is a high-leverage role for a builder-leader who can grow strong engineers, drive technical execution, and raise the bar on reliability, performance, security, and developer velocity.

This is not a pure operations role. Core Infrastructure at Harvey is responsible for building new systems as well as hardening existing ones, with an emphasis on architecture, scale, and long-term platform leverage rather than reactive firefighting alone.

Harvey is in a build era, not a maintenance era. New product surfaces ship rapidly, and India engineering is expected to play a foundational role in shaping the architecture, culture, and roadmap of Harvey’s next decade.

At Harvey, we value Decisiveness, Simplicity, and the mindset that Job's Not Finished. We move fast, prioritize clarity, and are always striving for excellence. If this resonates with you, we'd love to hear from you.

Why This Role Matters:

Core Infrastructure exists to “deliver core infrastructure that powers our products and teams,” and its current mission is operational excellence at scale. The team serves two critical user groups: external customers who need Harvey to be as reliable as the tools it replaces, and internal product engineering teams who need infrastructure they can build on without firefighting.

The systems this team owns are directly tied to Harvey’s next wave of growth, including agent infrastructure, database resilience, site reliability, vector search, job execution, regional data residency, and multi-cloud scale.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead, hire, and develop a high-agency infrastructure team in Bengaluru, creating a culture of accountability, technical excellence, and strong mentorship.

  • Own delivery for core infrastructure investments spanning cloud infrastructure, observability, container orchestration, reliability, and platform foundations.

  • Partner closely with Product Engineering, Security, and adjacent platform teams so infrastructure accelerates product delivery instead of constraining it.

  • Guide technical strategy across multi-cloud infrastructure, including Azure- and GCP-based systems, Kubernetes orchestration, networking, container management, and infrastructure as code.

  • Drive operational excellence through better observability, incident response, disaster recovery, runbooks, alerting, and recovery tooling.

  • Help the organization scale safely by improving system design quality, hardening critical paths, and pushing durable solutions to reliability bottlenecks before they become customer-facing failures.

  • Partner with AI and product teams to support Harvey’s next major product surfaces, including agent workflows, model infrastructure, and large-scale document processing systems.

  • Contribute as a hands-on technical leader when needed, especially in architecture reviews, incident leadership, prioritization, and high-stakes cross-functional programs.

Representative Problems You May Lead:

  • Hardening the Agent Platform so product teams can ship AI agent experiences with resource isolation, authenticated sandbox access, and resilient execution.

  • Improving database resilience and recovery so incidents are mitigated quickly and the main database never becomes the bottleneck during critical events.

  • Raising site reliability through stronger alerting, failover strategy, autoscaling, and runbooks so customers are never the first to know Harvey is degraded.

  • Scaling vector and retrieval infrastructure that underpins document-heavy workflows and enterprise search, including migrations that improve reliability and unlock new capabilities.

  • Building a multi-region, enterprise-grade platform that meets strict data residency, security, and uptime expectations for global customers.

What We’re Looking For:

  • 4+ years of engineering management experience and 10+ years of hands-on infrastructure or platform engineering experience in production environments.

  • Deep technical strength across cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, networking, observability, CI/CD, and infrastructure-as-code tooling such as Terraform or Pulumi.

  • A track record of designing and scaling reliable distributed systems, with strong judgment around performance, fault tolerance, and operational tradeoffs.

  • Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives and translating ambiguous platform needs into clear execution plans and measurable outcomes.

  • Strong people leadership: hiring well, coaching engineers, creating accountability, and building a healthy, high-performing team culture.

  • Clear communication and calm execution during incidents, escalations, and high-stakes customer-impacting situations.

  • A systems mindset, bias for simplicity, and the ability to raise standards while keeping teams moving fast.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with AI/ML infrastructure, high-throughput inference systems, or model platform reliability.

  • Experience operating multi-tenant, security-sensitive platforms for enterprise or regulated customers.

  • Familiarity with Azure at scale; GCP or AWS experience also transfers well.

  • Experience supporting global, follow-the-sun operations or building teams across regions.

Additional Information

  • Work eligibility: Must be authorized to work in India. Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

Please find the Applicant Privacy for this region here.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We are hiring a Partner Manager to help operationalize and scale Harvey’s legal partnerships. This role will own the day-to-day management and execution of legal partnerships, ensuring each one translates into a clear, repeatable go-to-market motion.

You will work closely with Harvey’s legal partners and internal teams across Sales, Enablement, and Customer Success to develop joint GTM plans, enable partner teams, coordinate customer opportunities, establish governance and operating cadences, and track performance against shared goals.

The ideal candidate is a strong, detail-oriented operator who can bring structure to complex partnerships, drive cross-functional execution, and ensure partners are engaged and delivering measurable commercial value. They are equally comfortable managing strategic partner relationships and owning the operational work required to make those partnerships successful.

What You'll Do

  • Manage the day-to-day execution of select partnerships, including partner onboarding, enablement, joint planning, and ongoing program management.

  • Build strong working relationships with partner stakeholders and serve as a consistent point of contact across active initiatives.

  • Coordinate across cross-functional teams like Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Operations, Finance, Legal, and Product to ensure partner commitments are executed effectively.

  • Develop clear project plans, operating cadences, partner materials, and internal processes that make partnership programs scalable and repeatable.

  • Track partner activity, pipeline, engagement, and program performance, and provide clear updates to internal stakeholders.

  • Drive partner sourced pipeline to achieve pipeline generation targets and company goals.

  • Gather feedback from partners, customers, and internal teams to improve existing programs and inform future partnership strategy.

  • Support partner-facing meetings, business reviews, training sessions, and executive updates

What You Have

  • 5-7 years of professional experience in partnerships, consulting, business operations, strategy, sales, customer success, or a related field.

  • High attention to detail and a strong sense of ownership.

  • Strong program management skills, including the ability to manage multiple workstreams, establish clear owners and timelines, and drive follow-through from planning through execution.

  • Proven ability to build strong relationships with external stakeholders.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information and communicate clear recommendations.

  • Strong business judgment and the ability to operate effectively in ambiguous situations.

  • Ability to influence and maintain momentum across teams with competing priorities.

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth, and highly collaborative environment.

Compensation

$160,000 - $220,000 USD

Role Overview

Harvey is hiring a M&A Counsel to execute on complex, high-impact M&A transactions , while supporting adjacent corporate and partnerships legal needs.

This role is ideal for an experienced M&A lawyer who can own and drive M&A work streams end-to-end with minimal oversight, build Harvey’s M&A playbook and design scalable, AI-forward legal processes, and partner cross-functionally to execute Harvey’s acquisition strategy.

What You'll Do

  • Execute on M&A and other strategic transactions, including due diligence, structuring deal structures and term sheets, drafting and reviewing definitive agreements and negotiating key legal and business terms, managing signing, closing and post-closing integration, and overseeing outside counsel

  • Design, implement, and continuously improve scalable legal processes, templates, and playbooks to drive efficiency, consistency, and best practices across M&A and other strategic transactions

  • Act as a trusted business partner to stakeholders across the company, including Corp Dev, Finance, People, Product, and Operations

  • Support adjacent corporate matters as needed, including entity management, employment and compensation, real estate, and insurance

What You Have

  • JD degree and licensed to practice in either California or New York in good standing

  • 4-6+ years of relevant legal experience in M&A transactions and the ability to flex across adjacent corporate matters

  • At least 4 years in the M&A group of a top-tier law firm, preferably as a 5th year+ associate and with buy-side experience representing fast-growing technology companies

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment, manage competing priorities, and think creatively and strategically under tight timelines

  • Team-focused and collaborative working style; strong sense of ownership and comfort operating independently in a rapidly evolving practice

  • Exceptional communication skills and intellectual curiosity, with the ability to drive stakeholder alignment, exercise sound judgment and provide solutions-oriented legal advice

Compensation

$220,000 - $270,000 USD

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey is hiring a M&A Counsel to execute on complex, high-impact M&A transactions , while supporting adjacent corporate and partnerships legal needs.

This role is ideal for an experienced M&A lawyer who can own and drive M&A work streams end-to-end with minimal oversight, build Harvey’s M&A playbook and design scalable, AI-forward legal processes, and partner cross-functionally to execute Harvey’s acquisition strategy.







WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Execute on M&A and other strategic transactions, including due diligence, structuring deal structures and term sheets, drafting and reviewing definitive agreements and negotiating key legal and business terms, managing signing, closing and post-closing integration, and overseeing outside counsel

 - Design, implement, and continuously improve scalable legal processes, templates, and playbooks to drive efficiency, consistency, and best practices across M&A and other strategic transactions

 - Act as a trusted business partner to stakeholders across the company, including Corp Dev, Finance, People, Product, and Operations

 - Support adjacent corporate matters as needed, including entity management, employment and compensation, real estate, and insurance







WHAT YOU HAVE

 - JD degree and licensed to practice in either California or New York in good standing

 - 4-6+ years of relevant legal experience in M&A transactions and the ability to flex across adjacent corporate matters

 - At least 4 years in the M&A group of a top-tier law firm, preferably as a 5th year+ associate and with buy-side experience representing fast-growing technology companies

 - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment, manage competing priorities, and think creatively and strategically under tight timelines

 - Team-focused and collaborative working style; strong sense of ownership and comfort operating independently in a rapidly evolving practice

 - Exceptional communication skills and intellectual curiosity, with the ability to drive stakeholder alignment, exercise sound judgment and provide solutions-oriented legal advice







COMPENSATION

$220,000 - $270,000 USD

jobs.title: Staff Web Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

 

Role Overview

The Staff Web Developer joins Harvey's Web team as the senior technical leader for the architecture, data foundations, and systems integration behind harvey.ai and every web-facing surface. The team's mission is to make Harvey's web presence evolve at the velocity of the product itself — reliable, observable, and fast enough that Marketing and GTM can ship without waiting on engineering.

This role owns the technical strategy for that platform: the Next.js and Sanity architecture, the integration layer connecting the website to Harvey's marketing, analytics, and GTM systems, and the automation and testing practices the team currently lacks. You will be the most senior engineer on a small, front-end-leaning team, setting standards and mentoring as much as building.

You partner directly with Harvey's product engineering, security, and infrastructure organizations to make sure the web platform meets the same bar as the rest of the company. It is a rare opportunity to build foundational systems from scratch at one of the fastest-growing AI companies, with unusually direct line of sight from your work to the company's growth.

 

What You'll Do

  • Own the architecture of Harvey's web platform end to end — the Next.js/Vercel application, the Sanity content layer, and the services and APIs behind them — with a focus on reliability, performance, and scalability.

  • Design and build the data foundations and integration patterns that connect the website to Harvey's marketing, analytics, CRM, and GTM systems, supporting both real-time and batch workloads.

  • Establish automation, CI/CD, preview/deploy tooling, and robust automated testing where little exists today, reducing operational toil and increasing team velocity.

  • Set observability standards — structured logging, tracing, Core Web Vitals and performance budgets, alerting — so the team can catch and resolve issues before Marketing does.

  • Lead how the team applies AI and ML to web workflows, from content operations to personalization to internal tooling, and act as the bridge between product engineering and web engineering.

  • Partner with Security and Infrastructure to harden the platform without slowing developer experience.

  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to a small, front-end-focused team through code review, design review, and architectural guidance.

 

What You Have

  • 8+ years of Web Development experience with deep back-end and systems expertise, and a track record of owning technical architecture at a staff level of scope and ambiguity.

  • Strong command of the modern web stack — React/Next.js, TypeScript, and server-side rendering — paired with genuine back-end depth (Node, Python, or comparable) rather than front-end specialization alone.

  • Experience architecting and operating headless CMS and content platforms (Sanity, Contentful, or similar) at scale, including schema design and publishing workflows.

  • Proven experience building and operating reliable production systems: CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, observability tooling, and performance optimization against real user metrics.

  • Fluency with data infrastructure fundamentals — SQL/NoSQL databases, caching, queuing, API and webhook integration patterns — in service of marketing and GTM systems.

  • Experience integrating AI/ML capabilities into production web experiences or content workflows.

  • Demonstrated ability to mentor less experienced engineers, influence across functions, and operate autonomously in a small team where you are the deepest technical voice.

Nice to have: Vercel platform experience; marketing/GTM systems integration (HubSpot, Salesforce, Segment, analytics); SEO and web performance engineering; prior experience as the first or most senior engineer on a web platform team.

 

Compensation

$220,000-260,000 USD

 

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

jobs.title: Integrated Campaigns Lead
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey's users are among the most sophisticated professionals - from managing partners and practice leaders at global law firms to GCs and legal operations executives in-house, and tax and finance leaders adopting AI across their organizations.

These professionals are navigating a fundamental shift in how their work gets done. Reaching them starts with deeply understanding the realities of that work: the problems worth solving, the outcomes that matter, and the questions and skepticism that come with adopting AI. Our best campaigns turn that understanding into ideas and experiences that are useful, credible, and relevant to where each audience is on that journey.

The Integrated Campaigns Lead will build the function responsible for doing exactly that.You'll set Harvey's global integrated campaign strategy: defining our priority audiences, sharpening how we position Harvey, and designing coordinated programs that build awareness, deepen engagement, and drive growth. You'll establish the campaign operating model, prove what works, and build the team and capabilities to scale it globally.

This is a strategic player-coach role with meaningful influence across the company. You'll shape go-to-market priorities alongside leadership across marketing, product, GTM, and you'll stay close enough to the work to write the message, understand the data, and improve the campaign when it matters.

What You'll Do

  • Set Harvey's global integrated campaign strategy. Define the audiences, segments, narratives, and campaign architecture that build relevance with our audiences and drive awareness, engagement, pipeline, and revenue.

  • Turn audience insight into differentiated positioning. Develop messaging rooted in primary research, customer insight, competitive intelligence, and demonstrated use cases. Build claims on evidence and create narratives sophisticated audiences find credible.

  • Translate company priorities into market-facing programs. Partner with Product, Sales, and business leaders to develop marketing strategies around Harvey's most important growth initiatives, connecting what matters to the business with what matters to our audiences.

  • Orchestrate the full marketing system. Bring together digital, social, communications and analyst relations, alliances, events, field marketing, and other channels into cohesive global campaigns, spanning major launches, category-building moments, and always-on programs.

  • Build the measurement system. Define the KPIs, dashboards, attribution signals, and operating cadence that connect campaign investment to audience and business outcomes.

  • Build the team and operating model. Design how the campaigns function works, hire exceptional marketers, and develop them into strategic owners of audiences, programs, and business outcomes.

  • Raise the creative and strategic bar. Establish what great campaign thinking looks like at Harvey, from the quality of the insight and sharpness of the message to the craft of the execution and rigor of the measurement.

  • Build an AI-native campaign engine. Apply AI across audience research and modeling, creative development, experimentation, personalization, localization, and performance analysis. Develop repeatable approaches that raise the capabilities of the broader marketing organization.

What You Have

  • 8+ years of B2B marketing experience, including significant ownership of integrated campaigns, demand generation, or go-to-market programs within enterprise software or high-growth SaaS.

  • A record of building and scaling. You've created teams, programs, or operating models and know how to introduce structure without introducing unnecessary process.

  • Experience building and leading exceptional teams. You've hired, developed, and retained high-performing marketers.

  • Strong commercial instincts. You've owned multi-million-dollar investments and understand how to connect marketing decisions to audience impact, pipeline, revenue, and ROI.

  • Exceptional positioning and messaging judgment. You know how to get from audience research and market insight to a differentiated point of view, and you're a strong enough writer to do the work yourself when the stakes are high.

  • Exceptional cross-functional influence. You've orchestrated digital, social, communications, analyst relations, partnerships, events, and field marketing as one system rather than optimizing a single channel in isolation.

  • Hands-on fluency with AI. AI is already part of your campaign workflow. You have informed opinions about where it meaningfully improves marketing, and where human judgment remains the advantage.

  • A player-coach operating style. You're comfortable setting strategy with senior leaders and equally comfortable opening the doc, digging into the dashboard, rewriting the brief, or working through the details with the team.

  • Comfort with ambition and ambiguity. You can create clarity where there isn't yet a playbook, move quickly without lowering the bar, and build systems that become more sophisticated as Harvey grows.

Compensation

$196,000 - $269,500 USD

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

You'll set Harvey's global integrated campaign strategy: defining our priority audiences, sharpening how we position Harvey, and designing coordinated programs that build awareness, deepen engagement, and drive growth. You'll establish the campaign operating model, prove what works, and build the team and capabilities to scale it globally.



This is a strategic player-coach role with meaningful influence across the company. You'll shape go-to-market priorities alongside leadership across marketing, product, GTM, and you'll stay close enough to the work to write the message, understand the data, and improve the campaign when it matters.







WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Set Harvey's global integrated campaign strategy. Define the audiences, segments, narratives, and campaign architecture that build relevance with our audiences and drive awareness, engagement, pipeline, and revenue.

 - Turn audience insight into differentiated positioning. Develop messaging rooted in primary research, customer insight, competitive intelligence, and demonstrated use cases. Build claims on evidence and create narratives sophisticated audiences find credible.

 - Translate company priorities into market-facing programs. Partner with Product, Sales, and business leaders to develop marketing strategies around Harvey's most important growth initiatives, connecting what matters to the business with what matters to our audiences.

 - Orchestrate the full marketing system. Bring together digital, social, communications and analyst relations, alliances, events, field marketing, and other channels into cohesive global campaigns, spanning major launches, category-building moments, and always-on programs.

 - Build the measurement system. Define the KPIs, dashboards, attribution signals, and operating cadence that connect campaign investment to audience and business outcomes.

 - Build the team and operating model. Design how the campaigns function works, hire exceptional marketers, and develop them into strategic owners of audiences, programs, and business outcomes.

 - Raise the creative and strategic bar. Establish what great campaign thinking looks like at Harvey, from the quality of the insight and sharpness of the message to the craft of the execution and rigor of the measurement.

 - Build an AI-native campaign engine. Apply AI across audience research and modeling, creative development, experimentation, personalization, localization, and performance analysis. Develop repeatable approaches that raise the capabilities of the broader marketing organization.







WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 8+ years of B2B marketing experience, including significant ownership of integrated campaigns, demand generation, or go-to-market programs within enterprise software or high-growth SaaS.

 - A record of building and scaling. You've created teams, programs, or operating models and know how to introduce structure without introducing unnecessary process.

 - Experience building and leading exceptional teams. You've hired, developed, and retained high-performing marketers.

 - Strong commercial instincts. You've owned multi-million-dollar investments and understand how to connect marketing decisions to audience impact, pipeline, revenue, and ROI.

 - Exceptional positioning and messaging judgment. You know how to get from audience research and market insight to a differentiated point of view, and you're a strong enough writer to do the work yourself when the stakes are high.

 - Exceptional cross-functional influence. You've orchestrated digital, social, communications, analyst relations, partnerships, events, and field marketing as one system rather than optimizing a single channel in isolation.

 - Hands-on fluency with AI. AI is already part of your campaign workflow. You have informed opinions about where it meaningfully improves marketing, and where human judgment remains the advantage.

 - A player-coach operating style. You're comfortable setting strategy with senior leaders and equally comfortable opening the doc, digging into the dashboard, rewriting the brief, or working through the details with the team.

 - Comfort with ambition and ambiguity. You can create clarity where there isn't yet a playbook, move quickly without lowering the bar, and build systems that become more sophisticated as Harvey grows.







COMPENSATION

$196,000 - $269,500 USD

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

As a Product Operations Manager, Data at Harvey, you'll be the connective tissue between our data product surfaces, Engineering, GTM, and the external technology partners we rely on — making sure customer and partner signals turn into fast, well-coordinated action. You'll own intake and triage for feature requests and data issues, run early-access programs and cross-functional launches, and manage the partner relationships that keep our data pipeline reliable for law firms and in-house legal teams pushing the frontier of AI adoption.

This is a role for someone who's comfortable being in the weeds of a technical issue one hour and briefing leadership on launch risk the next — and who'd rather build a lightweight system that scales than a heavy process that doesn't get used.

What You'll Do

Customer, Partner & Issue Intake — Making sure the right signal reaches the right team, fast

  • Own the intake, triage, and prioritization of customer feature requests.

  • Triage customer-reported data and product issues, assess severity and impact, coordinate resolution across the appropriate teams, and ensure timely communication.

  • Manage relationships with external technology partners, including onboarding, ongoing operations, issue resolution, and delivery quality.

Programs & Launches — Getting new capabilities into customers' hands, then out the door broadly

  • Plan and run early-access programs for new features, including customer selection, onboarding, feedback collection, usage analysis, and launch recommendations.

  • Coordinate cross-functional launches by tracking dependencies, validating operational readiness, surfacing risks, and keeping high-priority initiatives on track.

Systems That Scale — Turning feedback and recurring friction into durable process

  • Translate customer, partner, and internal feedback into clear requirements, prioritized workstreams, and actionable recommendations.

  • Create and maintain documentation, playbooks, and enablement materials that help internal teams communicate and operate effectively.

  • Identify recurring operational challenges and implement lightweight systems, automation, and processes that enable the team to scale.

What You Have

  • 3-5+ years in Product Operations, Program Management, Technical Program Management, or a related operational role at a high-growth tech or SaaS company — ideally supporting data, integrations, or technical product surface.

  • Experience triaging and prioritizing inbound requests and issues at volume — you know how to separate signal from noise and route things to the right owner without becoming a bottleneck.

  • Comfortable engaging with data and technical issues directly enough to assess severity and impact, even when you're not the one fixing them.

  • Experience managing external vendor or technology partner relationships, including onboarding and ongoing delivery quality.

  • Hands-on experience running early-access or beta programs and coordinating launches in a fast-moving product environment.

  • Strong written communication — you can turn messy feedback into clear requirements, playbooks, and documentation that other teams actually use.

  • Proven ability to drive cross-functional alignment across Product, Engineering, and GTM without direct authority.

  • A bias toward lightweight systems over heavy processes — you'd rather ship a simple fix that scales than a perfect framework nobody uses.

Compensation

$155,400 - $233,200 USD

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

Working closely with Marketing, Product, and GTM teams to define clear workflows, practical use cases, and repeatable, customer-ready assets across different segments and buyers. Success shows up as shared clarity across GTM, faster customer adoption and value realization, quality pipeline, and a durable story that scales as Harvey grows.

  • Regularly conduct market, customer, and competitive research, grounding positioning and strategy in real customer needs and differentiated value.

  • Align on solutions prioritization and market opportunity across Product, GTM, and Marketing leadership teams.

  • 6-8+ years of experience in Product Marketing, Solutions Marketing, or a related role in B2B SaaS.

  • Expertise in developing positioning and messaging, and translating it into sales-facing and customer-facing assets across different audiences, segments, and verticals.

$137,600 - $206,400 USD

Role Overview

Harvey’s Customer Experience team provides 24/7 support across AMER, EMEA, and APAC. As Harvey expands across customer segments and regions, the volume, location, and nature of that work will continue to change. At the same time, we are reshaping how much capacity we need and where we need it at rapid speed.

The Global CX Workforce Manager will build and own the workforce-planning function for our global support organization. You will translate customer growth and operational changes into clear forecasts, staffing plans, schedules, and investment recommendations, protecting our service-quality bar while ensuring we deploy capacity responsibly.

This is a hands-on builder role. You will establish the models, metrics, tools, and operating cadence yourself, then evolve them as the organization scales. Regional managers will continue to own their people, quality, and day-to-day execution; you will provide the global planning framework that allows those teams to operate as one connected organization.

What You’ll Do

  • Own demand and capacity forecasts across regions, shifts, customer segments, issue types, and support channels. Translate ticket volume, active handle time, service-level targets, occupancy, shrinkage, schedule adherence, time off, and new-hire ramp into clear staffing requirements.

  • Build and own the model that turns company trajectory into a defensible view of CX capacity, drawing on revenue and customer projections, product launches, regional expansion, and seasonality. Make that model an input to company planning rather than a downstream consumer of it.

  • Lead weekly, monthly, and quarterly capacity reviews, clearly explaining forecast changes, coverage gaps, assumptions, and recommended actions.

  • Establish global scheduling standards covering shift allocation, PTO, holidays, weekends, on-call coverage, and business continuity in partnership with regional managers.

  • Create scenario plans that show when, where, and at what level Harvey should hire, cross-train, change schedules, or redeploy existing capacity. Recommend the option that best balances customer impact, employee sustainability, speed, and cost.

  • Measure the capacity impact of AI and operational investments, including chatbot, routing improvements, provisioning automation, and evolving team responsibilities. Identify the operational changes that increase throughput or flexibility without lowering the bar for accuracy, professionalism, QA, or customer satisfaction.

  • Support the launch and ramp of new locations and staffing models through cohort planning, readiness criteria, and post-launch performance reviews.

  • Define consistent workforce metrics and partner with Data, Finance, People, Enablement, and GTM Operations to establish reliable reporting and dashboards.

  • Evaluate and implement workforce-management tooling as the organization’s complexity grows.

What You Have

  • 7+ years of experience in workforce management, capacity planning, support operations, or a related discipline.

  • Experience building or materially redesigning a workforce-planning function, not only operating within an established system.

  • Experience supporting a 24/7, multi-region operation with asynchronous ticket-based work; experience beyond traditional voice contact-center planning is important.

  • A track record of building useful models from incomplete or rapidly changing data and improving their accuracy over time.

  • Strong analytical skills and hands-on fluency with spreadsheets, reporting tools, and workforce data. Experience with SQL, BI tools, Zendesk, or workforce-management platforms is strongly preferred.

  • The judgment to distinguish a temporary coverage problem from a structural headcount need, and to recommend action before service quality deteriorates.

  • Experience measuring how automation, AI, self-service, and workflow changes affect staffing demand and productivity.

  • Strong cross-functional leadership skills and the ability to drive consistent global operating practices through regional leaders without owning their teams directly.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to turn complex assumptions and tradeoffs into concise recommendations for executives.

Nice to Have

  • Experience planning workforce capacity across enterprise, mid-market, and SMB customer segments.

  • Experience supporting a rapidly growing SaaS or AI company where historical demand is not yet predictable.

  • Familiarity with support quality, enablement, routing, and escalation programs in addition to core workforce management.

"This role is open to remote candidates located in: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, District of Columbia, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Louisiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Missouri, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin”

 

Compensation

$120,900 - $181,300 USD

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

As a Product Operations Manager, Integrations at Harvey, you'll own the operating system behind our integrations and partner ecosystem — the APIs, MCP servers, and third-party connectors that let law firms and in-house legal teams plug Harvey into the rest of their tech stack. You'll triage and prioritize integration requests, manage the technology and ISV partners building on our platform, run early-access programs for new integrations, and coordinate the launches that bring them to market — all while building the lightweight systems that let the integrations program scale as our partner ecosystem grows.

This is a role for someone who's spent real time inside an integrations team or a marketplace/app store business, understands what makes an API- or MCP-based integration actually hold up in production, and knows how to balance partner needs against Harvey's own roadmap and security bar.

What You'll Do

Partner & Integration Request Intake — Making sure the right signal reaches the right team, fast

  • Own the intake, triage, and prioritization of integration and API/MCP feature requests from customers and partners.

  • Triage partner- and customer-reported integration issues, assess severity and impact, coordinate resolution across the appropriate teams, and ensure timely communication.

  • Manage relationships with technology and ISV partners across the integration lifecycle — onboarding, ongoing operations, issue resolution, and delivery quality.

Programs & Launches — Getting new integrations into partners' and customers' hands, then out the door broadly

  • Plan and run early-access programs for new integrations and API/MCP capabilities, including partner selection, onboarding, feedback collection, usage analysis, and launch recommendations.

  • Coordinate cross-functional launches of new integrations by tracking dependencies, validating operational readiness, surfacing risks, and keeping high-priority initiatives on track.

Systems That Scale — Turning feedback and recurring friction into durable process

  • Translate partner, customer, and internal feedback into clear requirements, prioritized workstreams, and actionable recommendations for the integrations roadmap.

  • Create and maintain documentation, playbooks, and enablement materials — including partner-facing API/MCP documentation — that help internal teams and partners communicate and operate effectively.

  • Identify recurring operational challenges in the partner and integration lifecycle, and implement lightweight systems, automation, and processes (partner onboarding checklists, certification criteria, listing standards) that let the program scale.

What You Have

  • 3-5+ years in Product Operations, Program Management, Partner or Ecosystem Operations, or a related role at a high-growth tech or SaaS company — ideally on a team responsible for integrations, APIs, or a partner platform.

  • Direct experience working on an integrations team — you've sat inside the function that builds, ships, and supports third-party connections, not just consumed them.

  • Working knowledge of APIs and MCP (Model Context Protocol) — comfortable in conversations about auth, rate limits, schemas, and what separates a reliable integration from a fragile one.

  • Experience from an app store, marketplace, or partner ecosystem business — managing listings, partner certification, marketplace policies, or developer relations — so you understand both sides of a two-sided platform.

  • Experience managing external technology or ISV partner relationships, including onboarding and ongoing delivery quality.

  • Hands-on experience running early-access or beta programs and coordinating launches in a fast-moving product environment.

  • Strong written communication — you can turn partner and customer feedback into clear requirements, playbooks, and documentation that both internal and partner teams actually use.

  • Proven ability to drive cross-functional alignment across Product, Engineering, Partner/BD and GTM without direct authority.

  • A bias toward lightweight systems over heavy processes — you'd rather ship a simple fix that scales than a perfect framework nobody uses.

Compensation

$155,400 - $233,200 USD

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

 - Manage relationships with technology and ISV partners across the integration lifecycle — onboarding, ongoing operations, issue resolution, and delivery quality.

Programs & Launches — Getting new integrations into partners' and customers' hands, then out the door broadly

 - Plan and run early-access programs for new integrations and API/MCP capabilities, including partner selection, onboarding, feedback collection, usage analysis, and launch recommendations.

 - Coordinate cross-functional launches of new integrations by tracking dependencies, validating operational readiness, surfacing risks, and keeping high-priority initiatives on track.

Systems That Scale — Turning feedback and recurring friction into durable process

 - Translate partner, customer, and internal feedback into clear requirements, prioritized workstreams, and actionable recommendations for the integrations roadmap.

 - Create and maintain documentation, playbooks, and enablement materials — including partner-facing API/MCP documentation — that help internal teams and partners communicate and operate effectively.

 - Identify recurring operational challenges in the partner and integration lifecycle, and implement lightweight systems, automation, and processes (partner onboarding checklists, certification criteria, listing standards) that let the program scale.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 3-5+ years in Product Operations, Program Management, Partner or Ecosystem Operations, or a related role at a high-growth tech or SaaS company — ideally on a team responsible for integrations, APIs, or a partner platform.

 - Direct experience working on an integrations team — you've sat inside the function that builds, ships, and supports third-party connections, not just consumed them.

 - Working knowledge of APIs and MCP (Model Context Protocol) — comfortable in conversations about auth, rate limits, schemas, and what separates a reliable integration from a fragile one.

 - Experience from an app store, marketplace, or partner ecosystem business — managing listings, partner certification, marketplace policies, or developer relations — so you understand both sides of a two-sided platform.

 - Experience managing external technology or ISV partner relationships, including onboarding and ongoing delivery quality.

 - Hands-on experience running early-access or beta programs and coordinating launches in a fast-moving product environment.

 - Strong written communication — you can turn partner and customer feedback into clear requirements, playbooks, and documentation that both internal and partner teams actually use.

 - Proven ability to drive cross-functional alignment across Product, Engineering, Partner/BD and GTM without direct authority.

 - A bias toward lightweight systems over heavy processes — you'd rather ship a simple fix that scales than a perfect framework nobody uses.







COMPENSATION

$155,400 - $233,200 USD

Role Overview

As a Senior Product Operations Manager at Harvey, you will be the connective tissue between Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market teams — turning strategy into execution across our entire product lifecycle. You'll build and scale the operating systems that help our product teams make better decisions, ship with confidence, and drive measurable impact for law firms and in-house legal teams pushing the frontier of AI adoption.

You'll work as an extension of product leadership, balancing hands-on execution with strategic initiatives. This is a role for someone who builds from 0 to 1, thrives in ambiguity, and creates structure where none exists.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Inputs to Product Teams — Ensuring teams have the information they need to make great decisions

    • Build and maintain Voice of Customer systems that synthesize feedback from law firm partners, in-house clients, CSMs, and sales into actionable product signals

    • Establish rigorous mechanisms for measuring product success and user impact, including analytics dashboards, KPIs, and clear hypotheses

    • Create high-leverage engagement points with customers and partners throughout the product lifecycle — from alpha through post-GA

    • Streamline key decision points across teams, reducing friction and improving prioritization quality

    Ops of the Product Org — Creating the operating systems that enable product teams to thrive

    • Own and improve core product development processes, tooling, and team rituals (planning cycles, monthly reviews, roadmap prioritization, etc.)

    • Build reliable run-of-business systems that scale as Harvey grows — launch calendars, intake frameworks, RACI structures

    • Drive cross-functional alignment between Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success

    • Facilitate roadmap planning by coordinating stakeholder inputs and maintaining transparency across the org

    Outputs from Product Teams — Amplifying product impact by connecting what we build to those who need it

    • Design and run Early Access Programs and alpha testing programs that validate product-market fit and surface refinement signals before broad release

    • Own launch coordination end-to-end — ensuring timely, high-confidence rollouts with clear success metrics and post-launch monitoring

    • Maintain cross-team roadmap visibility that keeps GTM, Legal, and leadership aligned on what's shipping and why

    • Make it clear across Harvey what Product is building, how it's progressing, and what's coming next.

 

What You Have

  • 5+ years in Product Operations, Product Management, or a closely related operational role at a high growth tech or SaaS company

  • You've built processes and programs from scratch and scaled them thoughtfully — not just inherited and maintained them

  • Experience working with AI-native products, ideally in a domain where model quality and output reliability are central to the user experience

  • Strong ability to translate complex qualitative and quantitative data — usage metrics, feedback themes, retention signals — into clear recommendations and roadmap inputs

  • Proven ability to drive alignment across Product, GTM, and Engineering without direct authority

  • Hands-on experience with launch coordination, EAPs, or customer feedback loops in a fast-moving product environment

  • You're a natural bridge builder: fluent in strategy, comfortable in the weeds, and skilled at creating clarity where none exists. Ambiguity doesn't slow you down — it's where you do your best work.

 

Compensation Range

$155,400 - $233,200 USD

Role Overview

The Senior Brand Designer crafts how Harvey shows up across every touchpoint, translating a complex legal AI product into clear, compelling stories and systems. They sit on the Brand & Creative team, partnering closely with growth marketing, product marketing, content marketing and creative operations to ship high-impact work that’s cohesive and scalable. This role drives the evolution of Harvey’s brand system and campaigns so that every asset reinforces our position as the category-defining legal AI platform. They make key calls on creative direction within their projects and are a trusted collaborator to cross-functional partners. It’s a chance to help define a fast-moving brand from the inside, with direct line-of-sight to the impact of your work.

What You'll Do

  • Own end-to-end creative for priority initiatives — from brief to concept to launch — across social, product marketing, sales enablement and external events.

  • Evolve and extend Harvey’s brand system (visual language, layout, motion, and templates) so it’s recognizable, flexible, and easy for others to use.

  • Collaborate closely with PMM, marketing, and product partners to clarify goals, shape briefs, and turn complex ideas into simple, high-impact narratives and visuals.

  • Work hand-in-hand with creative operations and producers to scope projects, set milestones, and keep work moving smoothly from kickoff through delivery.

  • Give and receive clear, constructive feedback; help raise the quality bar for the broader creative team through critique, documentation, and mentorship of other designers.

What You Have

  • Significant experience in brand or marketing design roles (in-house or agency), including owning complex, multi-channel projects end-to-end.

  • A portfolio that demonstrates strong visual craft, systems thinking, and clear storytelling across campaigns, product marketing, and/or B2B tech or SaaS work.

  • Proven ability to collaborate with PMM, marketing, and other cross-functional partners, turning ambiguous briefs into focused creative directions.

  • Comfort working within and evolving a brand system — knowing when to extend patterns and when to introduce new ones thoughtfully.

  • Strong communication skills: you can explain the “why” behind your work, incorporate feedback, and advocate for the brand and audience effectively.

Compensation

$155,600 - $214,000 USD

Role Overview

Harvey's Sales Manager, Public Sector leads our go-to-market into United States federal, state, and local government legal organizations. This is a build role. You will recruit and lead a team of Enterprise Account Executives covering federal agencies and state and local government, and you will own the number for the segment — quota, pipeline, forecast, and execution. Harvey already has active engagements at government agencies; your job is to turn early momentum into a durable, repeatable government sales motion.

What You'll Do

  • Recruit, coach, and lead a team of Enterprise AEs across Federal and State & Local, including sourcing and closing the founding hires.

  • Own quota attainment, pipeline generation, and forecast accuracy for the Public Sector segment.

  • Build the public sector sales playbook from zero — qualification criteria, procurement path selection, security review sequencing, and fiscal-year timing.

  • Carry a small number of strategic accounts personally through the first two quarters while the team ramps.

  • Partner with the Head of Public Sector on channel strategy and on FedRAMP and StateRAMP/GovRAMP positioning.

  • Work cross-functionally with Legal Engineering, Security and Compliance, Legal, and Finance to move agency security reviews, authorizations, and contract vehicles forward.

  • Represent Harvey across the government legal and gov-tech community in Washington and in-market.

  • Travel as required, including agency sites and Harvey offices.


What You Have

  • 8–10+ years of technology sales experience, including 3–5+ years managing public sector sellers.

  • Personally carried and hit a public sector quota as an individual contributor before moving into management.

  • Experience standing up a public sector sales team, region, or territory from scratch — not advising or supporting one that already existed.

  • Fluency in government procurement: GSA schedules, GWACs, OTAs, sole-source and exemption pathways, FAR fundamentals, and state tender and cooperative purchasing processes.

  • Comfort with long, non-linear cycles and fiscal-year budget dynamics.

  • Ability to lead complex, multi-threaded sales spanning agency general counsel, CIO and CISO organizations, contracting officers, and end-user attorneys.

  • Genuine conviction about the mission and about equipping public servants with frontier technology.

Nice to Have

  • Existing relationships across federal agency legal, CIO, or CISO organizations.

  • Prior experience selling into legal departments.

  • Experience managing a government reseller or channel relationship.


Compensation

$400,000 - $440,000 USD OTE 50/50

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.
