Role Overview

As Harvey scales its pre-sales function across EMEA, we are hiring a Legal Engineer Manager to lead and grow the team in Paris. This role exists to provide senior leadership and strategic direction to a team of Legal Engineers who sit at the heart of Harvey's commercial motion - bringing legal credibility, product expertise, and consultative support to law firm and in-house prospects.

Harvey’s Legal Engineers are skilled lawyers from top-tier law firms who apply their legal experience to ensure that current and prospective customers understand how Harvey’s solutions enhance specific day-to-day workflows, working alongside Harvey’s Account Executives to support all aspects of our sales strategy. Legal Engineers build consultative relationships with law firm partners and associates and in-house attorneys at private equity firms and Fortune 500 companies, becoming trusted advisors on how Harvey’s AI solutions can make them more effective.

Similar to the way Solutions Architects secure the “technical win” in the sales process, Legal Engineers secure the “legal win” by performing in-depth customer discovery and education on Harvey’s solutions through targeted meetings and demos that resonate with the customer’s day-to-day workflows specific to their legal practice area.

Legal Engineers utilize their experience practicing law and their legal mindset to ask thoughtful questions to understand the needs of law firm and in-house attorneys, develop credibility, and then partner with Account Executives to educate them on Harvey’s value via large and small group sessions as well as one-to-one conversations.

What You'll Do

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Legal Engineers, setting clear performance expectations and building a high-trust, high-output team culture

  • Own the quality and consistency of Harvey's pre-sales legal engineering function, ensuring demos, discovery conversations, and deal support are delivered to the highest standard

  • Partner closely with Account Executives and GTM leadership to prioritise pipeline, develop deal strategy, and support conversion on complex or strategic opportunities

  • Engage with lawyers at prospective customers to understand and address their workflow challenges

  • Collaborate with Product and Marketing to ensure the team's field insights are feeding into positioning, roadmap, and go-to-market strategy

  • Lead product demonstrations tailored to the context of various law firm practice groups and in-house legal teams, asking questions to validate how Harvey can add value and then showcasing Harvey’s features and benefits relevant to each prospective client’s potential use cases.

  • Act as the “Voice of the Customer,” using your legal perspective to help the broader sales team to develop and implement more effective strategies and synthesize customer feedback for the product team through a legal lens.

  • Travel may be required from time to time, including visits to customer office locations and company offices.


What You Have

  • Qualified lawyer with 7+ PQE, with experience in a law firm or in-house legal environment

  • Must have prior experience managing a team, with a track record of developing talent and driving performance

  • Deep familiarity with legal technology and AI tools, with an ability to quickly develop and demonstrate platform expertise

  • Strong commercial instincts and the ability to engage credibly with senior stakeholders at law firms and in-house legal teams

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, with experience running training, workshops, or client-facing product sessions

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with a pragmatic, solutions-oriented approach

We are seeking an experienced US Payroll Manager to help manage and scale our US payroll operations to meet the tremendous growth of the company. The ideal candidate thrives in a high-growth start-up, is detail-oriented, and has excellent interpersonal and communication skills. This person will be someone who can perform the operational work efficiently while simultaneously building and scaling for future growth.

What You'll Do

  • Accurate and timely payroll processing for all employees, ensuring compliance with federal, state, and local regulations

  • Ensure payroll accuracy & timely processing

  • Review and approve termination checks

  • Collaborate with People Ops to manage the payroll components of employee benefits programs such as health, dental, vision insurance, retirement plans, and other company-sponsored benefits

  • Serve as a primary point of contact for Workday enhancements

  • Prepare and maintain accurate records for internal and external audits and assist with compliance audits as needed. Ensure the confidentiality and security of data, maintaining data integrity and accuracy of employee records

  • Assist with month-end close tasks related to payroll entries

  • Lead annual 401k audit and ensure funding recon is completed following each payroll

  • Perform quarterly Form 941 filings and state tax reconciliations

What You Have

  • 6+ years of payroll experience, preferably with 2+ years in a supervisory or managerial role.

  • Bachelors degree (Business or related preferred)

  • CPP highly preferred

  • Experience implementing or operating within a Workday HRIS environment

  • Experience with payroll accounting, tax, etc

  • Intermediate knowledge of excel, google sheets, etc.

  • Excellent communication and customer service skills

  • Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information with utmost professionalism.

  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast- paced environment.

  • Problem-solving attitude with the ability to adapt to changing requirements and work under pressure.

  • Sense of urgency around the US payroll process and comfort supporting multiple time zones

Compensation

$116,000 - $174,000 USD

jobs.title: Program Manager, Product Systems and Insights
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey ships fast, and our customers tell us constantly what's working and what isn't — through CSMs, support, sales, and early-access programs. Today that signal lives in a hundred places and reaches Product inconsistently, and the systems that let the EPD organization plan, review, and fix things at scale are still being built. You will own those systems: a single Voice of the Customer program that turns scattered feedback into structured, trusted input for every product team; a bug management process that gets defects triaged, prioritized, and resolved predictably; and the operating rhythm that keeps Engineering, Product, and Design aligned. You own the infrastructure and cadence; embedded Product Operations Managers own the interpretation and day-to-day judgment for their product areas.

What You'll Do

Voice of the Customer Program

  • Design and stand up the end-to-end feedback pipeline: intake from CS, Support, Sales, and EAPs into one structured system

  • Partner with RevOps to design & implement tooling; define the workflows that make submitting feedback the easy default for field teams

  • Set the weekly triage cadence and SLAs so every piece of signal is classified, routed, and visible

  • Build reporting that Product, GTM, and leadership actually read — volume, themes, trends, and what changed

  • Own the classification model: product area, matter stage, root cause (missing capability, defect, or usability friction)

  • Give Design and Research standing views into the signal that matters to them

Product Operating Rhythm

  • Design and run the core engineering, product & design rituals: planning cycles, roadmap reviews, design reviews, and monthly business reviews

  • Build the run-of-business systems that scale as Harvey grows — intake frameworks, RACI structures, decision logs, shared calendars

  • Facilitate roadmap planning by coordinating inputs across Product, Engineering, Design, and GTM and maintaining transparency across the org

  • Make it clear across Harvey what EPD is building, how it's progressing, and what's coming next

  • Own the end-to-end bug lifecycle: intake from Support and the field, severity definitions, triage, routing to engineering teams, and resolution tracking

  • Define severity and SLA standards that CS, Support, and Engineering all agree to and can see

  • Run the recurring bug review with engineering and product leads; escalate aging or customer-impacting defects

  • Report bug volume, aging, and resolution trends by product area, and connect defect signal back into the Voice of the Customer taxonomy

  • Close the loop with Support and CS so customers hear when their issue is fixed

What You Have

  • 5+ years in program management, product operations, or a related operational role at a high-growth tech or SaaS company

  • You've built processes and programs from scratch and scaled them — not just inherited and maintained them

  • Hands-on experience running bug triage or incident/defect management processes across Engineering and Support

  • Experience designing and facilitating product development rituals — planning, reviews, prioritization — with senior engineering and design leaders

  • Deep fluency with feedback, ticketing, and data tooling; you're comfortable owning a taxonomy and the systems that enforce it

  • Ability to translate messy qualitative and quantitative input into clear, structured outputs

  • Proven ability to drive alignment and adoption across CS, Support, Sales, Product, and Engineering without direct authority

  • Experience with AI-native or highly technical products is a plus

  • You create clarity where none exists, and you're energized by a blank slate

ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey ships fast, and our customers tell us constantly what's working and what isn't — through CSMs, support, sales, and early-access programs. Today that signal lives in a hundred places and reaches Product inconsistently, and the systems that let the EPD organization plan, review, and fix things at scale are still being built. You will own those systems: a single Voice of the Customer program that turns scattered feedback into structured, trusted input for every product team; a bug management process that gets defects triaged, prioritized, and resolved predictably; and the operating rhythm that keeps Engineering, Product, and Design aligned. You own the infrastructure and cadence; embedded Product Operations Managers own the interpretation and day-to-day judgment for their product areas.







WHAT YOU'LL DO


VOICE OF THE CUSTOMER PROGRAM

 - Design and stand up the end-to-end feedback pipeline: intake from CS, Support, Sales, and EAPs into one structured system

 - Partner with RevOps to design & implement tooling; define the workflows that make submitting feedback the easy default for field teams

 - Set the weekly triage cadence and SLAs so every piece of signal is classified, routed, and visible

 - Build reporting that Product, GTM, and leadership actually read — volume, themes, trends, and what changed

 - Own the classification model: product area, matter stage, root cause (missing capability, defect, or usability friction)

 - Give Design and Research standing views into the signal that matters to them


PRODUCT OPERATING RHYTHM

 - Design and run the core engineering, product & design rituals: planning cycles, roadmap reviews, design reviews, and monthly business reviews

 - Build the run-of-business systems that scale as Harvey grows — intake frameworks, RACI structures, decision logs, shared calendars

 - Facilitate roadmap planning by coordinating inputs across Product, Engineering, Design, and GTM and maintaining transparency across the org

 - Make it clear across Harvey what EPD is building, how it's progressing, and what's coming next

 - Own the end-to-end bug lifecycle: intake from Support and the field, severity definitions, triage, routing to engineering teams, and resolution tracking

 - Define severity and SLA standards that CS, Support, and Engineering all agree to and can see

 - Run the recurring bug review with engineering and product leads; escalate aging or customer-impacting defects

 - Report bug volume, aging, and resolution trends by product area, and connect defect signal back into the Voice of the Customer taxonomy

 - Close the loop with Support and CS so customers hear when their issue is fixed







WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 5+ years in program management, product operations, or a related operational role at a high-growth tech or SaaS company

 - You've built processes and programs from scratch and scaled them — not just inherited and maintained them

 - Hands-on experience running bug triage or incident/defect management processes across Engineering and Support

 - Experience designing and facilitating product development rituals — planning, reviews, prioritization — with senior engineering and design leaders

 - Deep fluency with feedback, ticketing, and data tooling; you're comfortable owning a taxonomy and the systems that enforce it

 - Ability to translate messy qualitative and quantitative input into clear, structured outputs

 - Proven ability to drive alignment and adoption across CS, Support, Sales, Product, and Engineering without direct authority

 - Experience with AI-native or highly technical products is a plus

 - You create clarity where none exists, and you're energized by a blank slate

$155,400 - $233,200 USD

What You Have

  • 5+ years of experience in solutions architecture, sales engineering, or similar externally facing technical roles, or a mix of software engineering and customer-facing technical roles.

  • Proven track record designing and implementing solutions for enterprise customers in SaaS, cloud, or AI/ML environments.

  • Experience partnering with Account Executives and post-sales teams (e.g., Customer Success, Account Management) to drive adoption, renewals, and expansion within enterprise accounts.

  • Meaningful experience engaging with executives and C-suite stakeholders, including presenting complex technical concepts in a way that supports strategic decision-making.

  • Comfort engaging with customer security, risk, and compliance stakeholders, ideally in a SaaS or AI platform context.

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate between technical and non-technical audiences and build trust with senior stakeholders.

  • Curiosity about AI and a desire to work in a fast-moving environment where products and customer use cases are evolving quickly.

Role Overview

We're looking for a Lead Product Owner, Finance Systems to own the systems and workflows that power Harvey's finance organization as we scale globally. This role sits at the center of our finance technology portfolio: NetSuite as the ERP core, Zip for procurement intake and approvals, Ramp and Brex for spend and card programs, and Metronome for usage-based billing. You'll help shape the roadmap across that portfolio, prioritize competing demands, and drive changes from discovery through deployment, all in an agile and high-growth environment.

You'll partner closely with Accounting, FP&A, Revenue Operations, Procurement, and Tax, as well as teams across Business Technology (where the Finance Systems team lives) and Security, to translate business needs into scalable, well-governed solutions. This role is as much advisory as it is technical and hands-on: you'll bring thought leadership to the finance org, sit with stakeholders to understand complex and often ambiguous business problems, solution design the tools and automations, and then execute hands-on in the toolstack.

What You'll Do

Familiarity with the adjacent areas matters more than equal depth in all three.

 - Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills at various levels of the business and technology organizations: adapting how you make a case depending on the audience, building alignment across cross-functional teams, and saying no to a request and explaining why. A track record of mentoring peers, setting technical standards, or being the expert others escalate to on hard problems.

 - Demonstrated ability to solve ambiguous, high-stakes process problems without an existing playbook, operating with a high degree of autonomy while knowing when to pull others in on high-impact decisions. Examples include international expansion and multi-entity or multi-currency complexity, or new product offerings where pricing, billing model, and revenue recognition treatment have to be designed together.

 - Deep understanding of leading and emerging trends in SaaS finance applications and architecture, including where automation and AI are truly driving innovation.

 - Direct experience implementing best practices around change management, regression and UAT planning, segregation of duties, and regulatory requirements, while increasing efficiencies.





COMPENSATION

$175,000 - $225,500 USD

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey is the AI platform trusted by the world's leading law firms and corporate legal teams, and one of the fastest-growing companies in AI. Now we're bringing that to asset management — and this role owns it. We're building the team that will define how the world's leading asset managers, private equity firms, and institutional funds adopt AI. This is a ground-floor opportunity to own a new vertical — we're still proving out this motion, which means the person who joins will help write the playbook.

What You'll Do

  • Develop and manage a named account list across asset management — private equity, venture, private credit, hedge funds, real assets, and institutional allocators (LPs) — and own the full sales cycle from prospecting through contracting and expansion.

  • Build and manage senior relationships across each firm's legal, compliance, and investment teams — typically anchored by a GC, CLO, or CCO — expanding into portfolio-company counsel over time. Understand how decisions get made in these organizations and navigate accordingly.

  • Lead complex, multi-threaded deals with stakeholders ranging from managing directors and general partners to day-to-day legal and compliance users — translating Harvey's AI capabilities into language that resonates with financial buyers.

  • Work closely with product and engineering to stay current on Harvey's capabilities and shape solutions around how asset managers actually work — contract review, due diligence, portfolio company support, regulatory workflows.

  • Conduct tailored demos and presentations that connect Harvey's product directly to the workflows and pain points specific to financial services buyers.

  • Document what works. This team is building the asset management playbook from scratch, and your learnings will directly shape how we scale the motion.


What You Have

  • Experience selling complex software or professional services into financial services (ideally asset management, private equity, or institutional funds). You understand how these firms are structured and how buying decisions get made.

  • Proven ability to run a global or named account relationship — you've been the person a firm calls, not just the person who closes a deal and moves on. Ideally you've navigated a fund relationship or portfolio company motion.

  • Background in enterprise software sales, management consulting, or a combination — we're intentionally mixing profiles on this team. If you've unlocked a major financial services account or come from a firm that advises these organizations, we want to talk to you.

  • Comfortable operating in a motion that's still being defined. You're a builder who can prospect independently, iterate on messaging, and contribute to the team's collective learning.

  • Genuine curiosity about AI and how it applies to knowledge-intensive work. You don't need a legal background, but you should be excited about what Harvey is doing and motivated to develop real fluency in the space.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey ships fast, and our customers tell us constantly what's working and what isn't — through CSMs, support, sales, and early-access programs. Today that signal lives in a hundred places and reaches Product inconsistently, and the systems that let the EPD organization plan, review, and fix things at scale are still being built. You will own those systems: a single Voice of the Customer program that turns scattered feedback into structured, trusted input for every product team; a bug management process that gets defects triaged, prioritized, and resolved predictably; and the operating rhythm that keeps Engineering, Product, and Design aligned. You own the infrastructure and cadence; embedded Product Operations Managers own the interpretation and day-to-day judgment for their product areas.

What You'll Do

Voice of the Customer Program

  • Design and stand up the end-to-end feedback pipeline: intake from CS, Support, Sales, and EAPs into one structured system

  • Partner with RevOps to design & implement tooling; define the workflows that make submitting feedback the easy default for field teams

  • Set the weekly triage cadence and SLAs so every piece of signal is classified, routed, and visible

  • Build reporting that Product, GTM, and leadership actually read — volume, themes, trends, and what changed

  • Own the classification model: product area, matter stage, root cause (missing capability, defect, or usability friction)

  • Give Design and Research standing views into the signal that matters to them

Product Operating Rhythm

  • Design and run the core engineering, product & design rituals: planning cycles, roadmap reviews, design reviews, and monthly business reviews

  • Build the run-of-business systems that scale as Harvey grows — intake frameworks, RACI structures, decision logs, shared calendars

  • Facilitate roadmap planning by coordinating inputs across Product, Engineering, Design, and GTM and maintaining transparency across the org

  • Make it clear across Harvey what EPD is building, how it's progressing, and what's coming next

  • Own the end-to-end bug lifecycle: intake from Support and the field, severity definitions, triage, routing to engineering teams, and resolution tracking

  • Define severity and SLA standards that CS, Support, and Engineering all agree to and can see

  • Run the recurring bug review with engineering and product leads; escalate aging or customer-impacting defects

  • Report bug volume, aging, and resolution trends by product area, and connect defect signal back into the Voice of the Customer taxonomy

  • Close the loop with Support and CS so customers hear when their issue is fixed

What You Have

  • 5+ years in program management, product operations, or a related operational role at a high-growth tech or SaaS company

  • You've built processes and programs from scratch and scaled them — not just inherited and maintained them

  • Hands-on experience running bug triage or incident/defect management processes across Engineering and Support

  • Experience designing and facilitating product development rituals — planning, reviews, prioritization — with senior engineering and design leaders

  • Deep fluency with feedback, ticketing, and data tooling; you're comfortable owning a taxonomy and the systems that enforce it

  • Ability to translate messy qualitative and quantitative input into clear, structured outputs

  • Proven ability to drive alignment and adoption across CS, Support, Sales, Product, and Engineering without direct authority

  • Experience with AI-native or highly technical products is a plus

  • You create clarity where none exists, and you're energized by a blank slate

Compensation

$155,400 - $233,200 USD

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

We're looking for an experienced, hands-on Field Marketing Manager to own and execute our field marketing strategy. You'll lead the planning and delivery of first-party and third-party events, regional activations, and integrated campaigns designed to drive pipeline, lead generation, and revenue impact across Australia and the wider Asia-Pacific region.

You'll own the regional event strategy end to end, from flagship industry conferences and executive roundtables to targeted client dinners, ensuring every touchpoint reinforces Harvey's position in the legal AI market. Working closely with sales leadership, Customer Success, and cross-functional partners across APAC, you'll deepen client relationships and translate field activity into measurable pipeline contribution and revenue. The role involves regular travel across Australia and the wider APAC region. It is a unique opportunity to build out a regional field marketing function at a company redefining how professionals work with AI.

What You'll Do

  • Develop and execute a regional field marketing strategy across Australia and APAC, aligned with Harvey's revenue goals and brand objectives.

  • Plan, manage, and deliver a portfolio of events, including industry conferences, client roundtables, webinars, and executive dinners, that generate qualified pipeline and accelerate deals.

  • Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Partnerships to identify target accounts, align on priorities, and design account-based marketing programs for the region.

  • Analyse event performance data and market insights to continuously refine strategy, improve ROI, and report results to leadership.

  • Manage the regional field marketing budget, vendor relationships, and logistics to ensure efficient resource allocation and maximum impact.

  • Travel regularly across Australia and the wider APAC region to deliver events, meet clients, and support in-market sales activity.

What You Have

  • 6+ years of experience in field marketing, event marketing, or demand generation, ideally within B2B technology, SaaS, or professional services.

  • Proven track record of planning and executing field marketing campaigns that drive lead generation and revenue growth.

  • Sound commercial acumen, with the judgement to prioritise the activity that creates real impact and the discipline to see it through.

  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to collaborate across sales, marketing, and executive leadership.

  • Analytical mindset with experience tracking KPIs such as pipeline contribution, event ROI, and lead conversion.

  • Willingness and flexibility to travel across the APAC region, including international travel.

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey is looking for a Strategic Sourcing Manager to join the Finance team and own sourcing for our engineering technology and software categories. You will report directly to the Head of Procurement, based in the San Francisco HQ office.

This role owns the commercial relationship with the vendors that support Harvey's product and engineering organization: cloud infrastructure, data platforms, security and observability tooling, developer platforms, and enterprise SaaS. You will run competitive sourcing events, negotiate pricing and terms that improve as Harvey scales, manage the renewal pipeline, and partner with Engineering, Security, Legal, and FP&A to get deals done without unnecessary friction. Harvey's spend is scaling fast, and our sourcing motion has to scale with it.

What You'll Do

Category Strategy & Sourcing

  • Own category strategy and the sourcing pipeline for cloud infrastructure, data platforms, security and observability tooling, developer tools, and enterprise SaaS

  • Lead end-to-end sourcing events (RFI/RFP, supplier evaluation, selection) for new technology purchases; maintain a competitive supplier landscape for each category

  • Analyze vendor pricing, usage patterns, and market benchmarks to identify opportunities to improve economics and reduce commercial risk

Commercial Negotiation & Contract Structure

  • Lead commercial negotiations with software and infrastructure vendors, including committed-spend, tiered, usage-based, and enterprise license agreements

  • Structure agreements that balance commitment, flexibility, and unit economics as Harvey's usage grows; right-size license counts and tiers to actual utilization

  • Drive redlines on MSAs, order forms, and DPAs in partnership with Legal, Security, and Privacy; own the deal from first proposal through signature in Zip

  • Support the Head of Procurement and Partnerships on strategic AI provider agreements with usage analysis, benchmark data, and contract administration

Stakeholder Partnership

  • Partner with Engineering and Finance to forecast demand, translate technical requirements into sourcing strategy, and turn Harvey's growth into negotiating leverage

  • Serve as the commercial point of contact for engineering leadership; engage early in build-vs-buy decisions and vendor evaluations

  • Coordinate Security, Legal, and Privacy review so that technology purchases move through intake at the speed the business needs

Renewals, Supplier Management & Reporting

  • Own the renewal calendar for technology and software vendors; prepare negotiation briefs, utilization analysis, and benchmark data ahead of each renewal

  • Manage supplier relationships through execution, utilization monitoring, escalations, and renewal; consolidate overlapping tools and eliminate shelfware; track savings and cost avoidance against target

  • Build AI-powered sourcing playbooks and tooling for redlining, negotiation prep, and benchmarking that raise throughput and deal quality across the team

What You Have

  • 4–7 years of strategic sourcing or procurement experience with a focus on technology and software categories

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey is bringing its AI platform to the U.S. federal government — defense and civilian agencies whose legal, acquisition, and program teams are asking how to adopt AI responsibly. You will be Harvey's first Solutions Architect dedicated to public sector: the technical lead on federal opportunities, the person who designs how Harvey is deployed securely inside government environments, and the one who writes the playbook the rest of the team will follow.

You will sit at the intersection of Harvey's platform, agency stakeholders (legal, IT, security, acquisition, and program offices), and our Security & Trust, Legal Engineering, Product, and Customer Success teams. This is an opportunity to help define how AI is adopted across the federal government and to build a flagship public-sector practice at one of the fastest-moving companies in applied AI.

What You'll Do

  • Lead technical discovery and solution design for federal prospects and customers — defense and civilian — working with legal, IT, security, acquisition, and program stakeholders.

  • Design, document, and defend secure, compliant architectures for Harvey in government environments, including Harvey's FedRAMP High environment, identity and access patterns, integrations, and data-handling requirements (CUI, records retention, auditability).

  • Own the technical thread on a focused portfolio of high-impact federal accounts, from first conversation through rollout, adoption, and expansion.

  • Be the field-facing technical partner to Security & Trust on agency security reviews — FedRAMP High controls, DoD Impact Levels, ATO and authorization boundaries, NIST 800-53 — and translate them for program owners and counsel.

  • Work with Legal Engineers and Customer Success Managers to turn agency workflows and legal or policy use cases into concrete solutions, reusable patterns, and implementation playbooks.

  • Be the public-sector technical voice back into Harvey, synthesizing field feedback to inform roadmap, evaluation criteria, deployment options, and government-specific documentation.

  • Represent Harvey's technical perspective in public-sector forums — customer workshops, working groups, and stakeholder briefings — helping agencies understand both the possibilities and the limits of current AI systems.

  • Build the public-sector Solutions Architecture playbook — qualification, security review, deployment patterns, and enablement — so the practice can scale beyond one person.


What You Have

  • 7+ years in solutions architecture, sales engineering, forward-deployed engineering, or a similar customer-facing technical role.

  • Direct experience selling to or supporting U.S. federal customers (Department of Defense and/or civilian agencies) at a SaaS or cloud provider, including navigating agency security reviews and procurement.

  • Working knowledge of federal compliance frameworks and how they shape deployment — FedRAMP, NIST 800-53, DoD Impact Levels, ATO processes — and the ability to explain them to CISOs and program managers alike.

  • Hands-on depth in SaaS security and identity architecture: SSO/SAML, SCIM, encryption and key management, data residency, audit logging.

  • Clear communication with technical and non-technical audiences — from program managers and attorneys to CISOs and enterprise architects — and credibility with senior public-sector stakeholders.

  • Hands-on engagement with modern AI systems (LLMs, prompt design, evaluation, deployment patterns) and a desire to help agencies adopt them responsibly.

  • Comfort operating in an emerging practice area: energized by ambiguity, willing to build new playbooks, motivated by real-world impact on public services.

Preferred

  • Prior government service or military experience.

  • Experience with Azure Government or other government cloud environments.

  • Experience selling through federal systems integrators or contract vehicles.

  • Background in legal, e-discovery, or other document-heavy enterprise workflows.


Compensation

$218,800 - $300,900 USD OTE with a 80/20 split

Location

Remote within Washington, DC area - travel approximately 25–40% to agency and partner sites.

Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

As a Customer Experience (CX) Specialist, you will be the first line of support for both internal teams and external customers. This role is designed for support professionals with prior customer-facing experience who thrive in fast-paced environments, are eager to keep growing, and are excited to contribute to Harvey's rapid growth.

You'll focus on managing a high volume of non-technical support tickets, ensuring a seamless experience for our users. Over time, you'll have the opportunity to expand your technical skills, gain exposure to more complex support workflows, and progress within our CX team.

This role is built for support professionals ready to deepen their foundation in a technical product environment.

What You'll Do

  • Act as the first point of contact for non-technical support inquiries, ensuring timely, empathetic, and accurate responses.

  • Exercise sound judgment on ticket routing; knowing when to resolve independently and when to escalate to a senior support specialist.

  • Own your queue: manage ticket volume against SLA targets without sacrificing response quality. Customers should always receive accurate, complete answers that reflect Harvey's standard of care.

  • Apply consistent, accurate ticket tagging and categorization to support team-wide reporting and trend visibility.

  • Maintain a strong working knowledge of Harvey's core product features to provide clear and effective guidance.

  • Follow established playbooks and macros with precision; flag gaps or inconsistencies so the team can improve them over time.

  • Contribute to FAQs, internal guides, and knowledge base articles that streamline support for recurring questions; surface content gaps when customer questions reveal missing or unclear documentation.

  • Partner with the Customer Education team to flag areas where self-serve content can reduce repeat contact volume.

  • Stay adaptable and proactive in a rapidly evolving startup environment, operating effectively even when processes or product features are changing quickly.

What You Have

  • 2 years of professional experience in customer support at a SaaS company in the technology industry.

  • Experience with customer support platforms (e.g. Zendesk, Salesforce) and working fluency with AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini); you use them, not just know of them.

  • Strong written communication skills; clear, professional, and appropriately calibrated to the audience, whether a law firm partner or an internal stakeholder.

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with competing priorities and limited process documentation.

  • High process consistency: you follow established workflows reliably and flag when something doesn't fit the playbook rather than improvising silently.

  • Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail, including disciplined ticket hygiene.

  • Comfort with ambiguity; you can make sound judgment calls and move forward without having every answer in front of you.

  • Growth mindset and eagerness to learn technical concepts over time, with a clear interest in building toward more complex support scope.

Compensation

$68,000 - $102,000 USD

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey is building an in-house media production capability for our most critical internal shows, and this is the engineering role at the center of it. The Broadcast Engineer will own the technical foundation of how Harvey captures, routes, and delivers video and audio — the studio and control room infrastructure, the IP signal fabric connecting our spaces, and the live execution of the company’s highest-visibility events. Today that work is a mix of well-run events and vendor-dependent infrastructure; the opportunity is to replace it with systems we design, understand, and can scale. This person will split their time roughly evenly between running shows and building the platform those shows run on, partnering closely with Corporate IT, Workplace, Brand, and Communications. The right person is equally credible in a rack room designing a Dante domain and in a headset calling a hybrid all-hands with the CEO on camera.

What You'll Do

  • Design, build, and maintain Harvey’s video and audio infrastructure — studio spaces, control rooms, IP signal fabric, routing, recording, and streaming delivery — and own the standards, documentation, and configuration records behind it.

  • Architect and administer audio-over-IP and video-over-IP transport: Dante audio networks (clock hierarchy and PTP, multicast and IGMP behavior, QoS) and NDI video workflows (discovery, switch and VLAN design, bandwidth budgeting), in partnership with Corporate IT.

  • Own technical execution for Harvey’s highest-visibility productions — all-hands, executive broadcasts, customer events, launches, and recorded content — from engineering design and rehearsal through show call and post-event review, while raising day-to-day reliability across conference rooms and hybrid meetings.

  • Establish and maintain color and audio standards across the production chain: camera matching and shading, LUT and color pipeline management, monitor calibration, loudness normalization, and consistent delivery specs across live, recorded, and distributed output.

  • Diagnose and resolve complex signal-flow, network, sync, and device faults under live conditions, and convert each incident into a documented fix, a redundancy improvement, or a monitoring check.

  • Evaluate and integrate new production systems, and manage integrators, rental partners, and vendors through specification, commissioning, and acceptance testing.

What You Have

  • 7+ years of hands-on broadcast, live production, or high-end corporate production engineering experience, including ownership of permanent installations rather than only event-by-event work.

  • Deep, demonstrable command of video and audio signal flow — SDI and HDMI, embedding and de-embedding, sync and genlock, reference and timing, gain structure, and systematic fault isolation across a full chain.

  • Production experience with Dante audio networking and NDI video workflows, grounded in the networking fundamentals each actually depends on — clocking and PTP, multicast and IGMP, VLAN and switch design, QoS, and latency and bandwidth budgeting.

  • Working knowledge of color science as applied to production: color spaces and gamma, log formats, LUT creation and management, camera matching and shading, and monitor calibration for consistent output.

  • Proven ability to run technical execution for live, high-stakes events — rehearsal, show call, redundancy planning, and calm, structured incident response with an audience watching.

  • Strong documentation and communication skills: clear system drawings and signal-flow diagrams, runbooks another engineer can follow, and the ability to explain technical constraints to executives and presenters without jargon.

Bonus Points

  • Experience designing or commissioning a studio, control room, or broadcast facility from empty space through first show.

  • Depth with production switchers, digital audio consoles, DSP platforms (Q-SYS, Yamaha), intercom systems, and camera control/shading systems.

  • Zoom Room & Neatpad provisioning, operation and maintenance.

  • Streaming and distribution experience: encoding, transcoding, CDN delivery, SRT/RIST/RTMP transport, and multi-destination distribution.

  • Automation and monitoring skills — scripting, control-system programming, configuration management, or building instrumentation that catches failures before a show does.

  • Certifications such as Dante Certification Level 3, Q-SYS Level 1 or 2, AVIXA CTS/CTS-D/CTS-I, or relevant networking credentials.

  • Experience supporting a fast-growing, multi-office, globally distributed company.

Compensation

$129,200- $177,700 USD

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

The Software Engineer, New Grad joins Harvey's Engineering team, working alongside experienced engineers to build the AI-powered systems that serve the world's leading law firms and enterprises. The team's mission is to deliver secure, intuitive, and high-performance application-layer experiences that turn frontier AI capabilities into real customer value. This role offers an accelerated path to ownership, contributing production code to features spanning retrieval, document intelligence, and workflow automation from day one. It is an opportunity to develop rapidly at the intersection of AI and professional services, with direct exposure to how engineers shape a category-defining product.

We're currently hiring new grads to start in 2027 across multiple teams and roles, including Frontend, Backend, Full-Stack, Infrastructure, and Applied AI roles. Your interests & experience will be factored into our team matching process, where you’ll have the opportunity to learn about teams across Harvey including Agents, Applied AI, Assistant, Enterprise, Infrastructure, Mobile, Vault and many others.

What You'll Do

  • Design, implement, and ship production-level code across the stack while maintaining high quality, reliability, and security standards. You'll use AI-assisted development tools daily, and you’ll own the quality of everything you ship—AI-generated or not.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams including AI Research, Legal Engineering, Product, and Design to translate problem statements into compelling product experiences.

  • Collaborate with your team through code reviews, technical design discussions, and engineering best-practice development alongside senior and staff engineers.

  • Experiment with and evaluate cutting-edge LLMs and AI systems, contributing to how Harvey's platform evolves.

  • Depending on your team, you could work on retrieval over large document collections, interfaces for collaborating with AI systems, multi-region compute infrastructure, enterprise agents, or secure systems for sensitive client data.

What You Have

  • Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, graduated either in Winter 2026 - Spring 2027.

  • Able to work from our New York or San Francisco office starting in January 2027 and beyond, based on your graduation schedule. Relocation support is available.

  • Previous internship experience is required.

  • Technical foundation. Strong proficiency in one or more languages (Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Java, Go, or similar) and solid general computer science knowledge.

  • Decisiveness. You have a bias toward action. You've built something start to finish in coursework, a personal project, or a past internship, and you know the difference between a decision you should make yourself and one worth getting feedback on. You'd rather move and correct course than stall.

  • Simplicity. You can explain a complex technical idea in plain language, whether or not the person you're explaining it to is an engineer. You look for the simplest solution that works, and you know when added complexity is worth it.

  • Job's Not Finished. You aren't satisfied when something merely works. You proactively seek out feedback, act on it, and keep pushing after the assignment is technically complete. Past internship experience at an early-stage startup is a plus.

  • AI Forward. Comfortable using AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and curious about building LLMs into your own coding workflow.

Compensation

$165,000-$181,500

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey's Finance Engineering team is the investment-side counterpart to our Legal Engineering team: former investment professionals who bring real deal experience to Harvey's prospects and customers. Forward Deployed Finance Engineers lead discovery, demos, pilots, trainings, onboarding, and custom builds alongside our AEs and CSMs. They translate real investment work into Harvey solutions, serving as the trust layer across the entire customer lifecycle, from the first pilot to the most complex, custom-built workflow.

Finance Engineers work on Harvey Deals, a new product built off of Harvey's acquisition of Benchmark. Harvey Deals is where investment teams run their deals — screening, underwriting, diligence, and committee materials — built in the firm's own templates and formats, with every figure traceable back to the document it came from. Harvey works with 150+ asset management firms and analyzes 178M+ documents each month; the Finance Engineering team is how that capability meets the way deal teams actually work.

Finance Engineers understand how investors think and work, and use that expertise to design, build, and refine solutions that hold up under live deal pressure. In doing so, they don't just drive adoption; they shape Harvey's product roadmap, ensuring every release is grounded in what investment teams actually need. It's a team built to make Harvey the platform investment teams can trust with their most important work.

This role is the first Finance Engineer dedicated to private credit. You will build the credit playbook — demo library, workflow templates, use cases — while running live pilots, and lead the credit practice as the team grows.

You may be asked to travel around 2–3+ times per month. Travel is always for a significant business need and typically is for 1–3 days at a time.

What you'll do

Forward Deployed Finance Engineers on the private credit team are former credit investors who left the desk to help build the future of how credit gets underwritten. Working closely with Account Executives, they engage with direct lenders, opportunistic and specialty finance managers, BDC managers, and insurer credit arms throughout the pre-sales process and stay with them well past it — leading pilots on live opportunities, guiding lenders through what's possible with AI, and sitting down with credit teams to build screening, underwriting, and credit committee workflows in the firm's own templates and formats.

The work is the work they did on the desk: lender presentation and CIM review; QoE read-throughs and data pack analysis; cash flow and leverage modeling; sizing and structuring; covenant and credit agreement review; credit memo drafting; and comps. It continues post-close into compliance certificate review, covenant tracking, amendment and waiver analysis, and quarterly portfolio reporting, so value compounds after the first deal. Along the way, Finance Engineers bring credit-team feedback back into the product, helping shape the future of Harvey.

What you have

  • 3+ years on the investment or underwriting team at a direct lender, private credit fund, BDC manager, or insurer private credit arm, with demonstrated ownership of live deal work: screening, underwriting, diligence workstreams, modeling, structuring, and drafting credit committee materials. Asset-based and specialty finance backgrounds are welcome. Leveraged finance, restructuring advisory, or rating-agency experience before the principal side is welcome, but principal-side deal execution is required.

  • Strong command of the documents and data that drive a credit decision — lender presentation and CIM, QoE and data pack, model, credit agreement and intercreditor, compliance certificates — and an instinct for where the numbers and the paper disagree.

  • Advanced Excel and financial modeling, comfort with prompting and agentic AI workflows, and a builder's instinct for turning a repeated manual process into a repeatable automation. Python, SQL, or experience building internal tools is a plus.

  • Executive presence and relationship-building skills, with the ability to establish credibility from analysts and associates through to partners and credit committee members.

  • Outstanding communication and presentation skills — comfortable leading a live demo, facilitating a workshop, or holding your own in a technical conversation about a covenant package or an underwriting assumption.

  • Deep curiosity about AI's potential to transform investment work, paired with a practical, solutions-oriented mindset and bias toward action.

  • Track record partnering with senior stakeholders to drive results, with curiosity for testing approaches and optimizing for customer outcomes.

  • Customer-facing or commercial experience (LP or investor relations, capital formation, banking coverage, business development) and/or hands-on experience using AI tools in an investment setting are pluses.

Compensation

• OTE $254,600 - $350,000 USD (75/25 Split) • Offers Equity

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey is looking for a driven, strategic, and entrepreneurial Sales Development Manager to build and lead our first SDR team on the ground in Australia and New Zealand. This is the first dedicated SDR leadership role in the region. You'll have a rare opportunity to build a foundational go-to-market programme from scratch, shaping how Harvey engages with the most forward-thinking law firms, professional services organisations, and in-house legal teams.

You'll own everything from hiring and onboarding to coaching and performance management. You'll partner closely with Sales, Marketing, and RevOps to design a scalable, repeatable pipeline generation engine. You'll also help shape Harvey's regional go-to-market strategy by refining targeting, messaging, and outbound programmes that resonate with the ANZ legal market.

If you're excited by the idea of building teams, developing talent, and driving impact at a fast-growing AI company transforming legal work, we'd love to meet you!

What You'll Do

  • Build the ANZ foundation. Hire, onboard, and develop Harvey's first SDR team in Sydney, and set the team's structure, operating cadence, and performance standards.

  • Own regional pipeline performance. Drive the team's contribution to pipeline across inbound and outbound channels, with an initial focus on enterprise law firms and in-house legal teams, in close alignment with ANZ sales targets

  • Set goals and own the metrics. Define team goals and KPIs, track performance weekly, and use the data to decide where the team focuses.

  • Partner cross-functionally. Work closely with Sales, Marketing, and RevOps to improve lead routing, campaign effectiveness, and pipeline conversion. Build shared goals, a consistent operating rhythm, and feedback loops across teams, such as AE feedback on lead quality.

  • Partner with Account Executives. Shape SDR-to-AE pairings and joint account planning so the team helps AEs break into complex enterprise accounts.

  • Stay nimble. Redeploy the team quickly as priorities change, whether that's event-driven campaigns, outbound sprints, or inbound surges, rather than locking reps into fixed roles.

  • Partner with local leadership. Stay close to the APAC sales team to understand where they see the biggest challenges and opportunities. Use that insight to set the team's priorities, working within the frameworks and structures provided by HQ.

  • Support every segment. Work with Enterprise, Mid Market, and SMB teams to break into new logos and build pipeline across the market.

  • Coach and develop SDRs. Deliver hands-on coaching through regular 1:1s, call reviews, and deal strategy sessions.

  • Design onboarding and enablement. Partner with GTM Enablement to create programmes that ramp SDRs quickly and build deep product, industry, and prospecting expertise.

  • Refine targeting and messaging. Continuously test and improve outbound strategies, messaging, and account targeting based on ICP fit and performance insights.

  • Leverage data and tools. Use Salesforce, Salesloft, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Gong, and ZoomInfo to track performance and optimise workflows.

  • Build a strong team culture. Foster a high-performance culture grounded in ownership, learning, and collaboration.

What You Have

  • A track record of building sales development teams from the ground up, ideally as a founding member of an SDR or BDR function in Australia.

  • Direct experience leading SDRs or BDRs in a high-growth, outbound-focused environment.

  • Hands-on experience running both inbound and outbound motions.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and rapid change. You're energised, not unsettled, when priorities shift, and you're excited to be the architect of something new.

  • Agency and independence. You're in tune with your local market and act on what the business needs, without waiting for direction from HQ.

  • The ability to influence without authority, navigate ambiguity, and advocate for your team across functions

  • A coaching-first leadership style. You invest in people, celebrate wins, and hold high standards with care.

  • A data-driven mindset, with the ability to analyse team performance, uncover insights, and iterate quickly.

  • Deep familiarity with modern sales development tools, and the ability to recommend and implement tech stack improvements.

  • Excellent communication skills and executive presence, both internally and externally.

  • A passion for AI, innovation, and the transformation of knowledge work, especially in professional services and legal.

Additional Information

  • Location: Sydney, NSW (Hybrid with flexibility)

  • Work eligibility: Must have valid Australian work rights; Harvey does not currently offer visa sponsorship for this role

What We Offer

  • Structured hybrid working arrangement: 3 days in our Sydney office, 2 days working from home

  • Health Coverage: Fully covered private hospital insurance, plus extras for dental, optical, physio, mental health, and more.

  • Family & Fertility Support: Support for fertility treatments, adoption, and surrogacy through Carrot.

  • Retirement & Security: Comprehensive coverage designed to support your long-term well-being.

  • Paid Leave: Paid annual leave, sick leave, and fully paid parental leave for all parents.

  • Wellness & Perks: Daily in-office lunch, wellness memberships through Wellhub, and monthly commuting support.

  • Professional Development: Annual support for courses, certifications, conferences, and books.

  • Remote Work Allowance: Monthly support for home office, internet, and phone expenses.

  • Harvey Holiday: After four years, enjoy a four-week paid sabbatical to rest, travel, or explore new experiences.

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

You'll turn launches, product news, and company thinking into sharp, native content across our owned channels and our employees' channels. When we amplify a moment, it should land everywhere our people and audiences are.

You'll also own Harvey's social communities day to day. That means managing DMs, comments, and mentions; moderating and growing our community spaces; sending questions and opportunities to the right teams; and starting conversations that draw people toward Harvey. This role combines craft and community. It's for someone who writes fast and well, runs engaged communities with care and good judgment, and understands that on social, the caption, the reply, and the timing are the work.

What You'll Do

  • Write scroll-stopping copy for Harvey's owned channels (LinkedIn, Instagram, X, and emerging platforms), tuned to what performs on each.

  • Write copy for employee and advocacy channels to power company amplification. Give the team ready-to-post language that makes company moments land while keeping a consistent Harvey point of view.

  • Turn a single launch or announcement into a set of channel-native posts, threads, and replies that work together across audiences.

  • Work closely with the Social Manager to plan, draft, and deliver social creative and campaign content.

  • Keep a steady content calendar that balances planned campaigns with timely, real-time posts.

Community Management

  • Own the social inbox: monitor and respond to DMs, comments, and mentions across Harvey's channels quickly, warmly, and with good judgment.

  • Build and maintain response guidelines, tone standards, and saved replies for common questions so Harvey's voice stays consistent at scale.

  • Set up and run triage and escalation paths. Route customer support issues, sales inquiries, press requests, partnership opportunities, and sensitive or legal matters to the right internal teams, and close the loop.

  • Moderate Harvey's social communities and comment sections. Enforce community guidelines and deal with spam, trolling, and negative sentiment calmly and consistently.

  • Proactively join relevant conversations across the legal, legal tech, and AI communities to build relationships, raise Harvey's profile, and spot opportunities.

  • Find, engage, and grow a network of customers, advocates, and creators. Highlight their stories and user-generated content where appropriate and approved.

  • Run social listening to track brand mentions, sentiment, competitor activity, and emerging trends, and share key insights with Marketing, Product, Comms, and Customer Success.

  • Act as the first line of defense on social for brand safety. Flag potential issues early and help carry out response plans during sensitive or fast-moving moments.

    Measurement and Optimization

  • Track and report on content performance and community health, including engagement, response times, sentiment, follower growth, and conversation volume.

  • Use performance and engagement data to sharpen content, hooks, and response approach over time.

  • Share recurring themes from the community, such as questions, feedback, and pain points, to inform content strategy, product messaging, and FAQs.

What You Have

  • 3+ years in social content, community management, or a similar role, ideally at a high-growth tech, AI, or legal-focused company, or in a fast-moving brand or agency environment.

  • Exceptional short-form writing and editorial judgment, with a portfolio of content and community engagement that earned attention.

  • Hands-on experience managing a brand's social inbox and online communities, including moderation, escalation, and response workflows.

  • A real feel for internet culture, online communities, and what makes content and conversations travel.

  • Range as a voice chameleon: you can write as the brand and for employees without losing the through-line.

  • Comfort living in the replies and handling DMs, comments, and mentions with speed, warmth, and good judgment, including difficult or sensitive exchanges.

  • Sound judgment about confidentiality, customer privacy, and when to escalate rather than respond.

  • Ability to move quickly on real-time moments while keeping quality and brand safety high.

  • Strong organization and follow-through. You can manage a high volume of conversations and requests without dropping threads.

  • Experience with social management, scheduling, and listening tools (e.g., Sprout Social, Hootsuite, Brandwatch, or similar).

  • Comfort using analytics and engagement data to decide what you write and how you engage next.

  • A collaborative approach and experience working across Marketing, Comms, Customer Success, Sales, and Legal.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in legal tech, enterprise SaaS, or similar B2B spaces.

  • Background in copywriting, journalism, or editorial.

  • Experience running an engaged personal or brand account.

  • Experience building or managing a professional community, advocacy program, or creator/ambassador program.

  • Experience supporting crisis or issues management on social.

  • Interest in AI and responsible communication.

Compensation

$112,000 - $154,000 USD

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Secure Execution
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

As a Staff Software Engineer on the Security Engineering team, you will join as a founding team member and build the security foundations that let Harvey put increasingly capable AI agents to work. You'll lead development of a platform for agents to perform security work, while shaping how agents are sandboxed across our product and internal platforms.

One of the central challenges is enabling models with advanced cybersecurity capabilities to discover and validate vulnerabilities automatically, including through authorized penetration testing, while protecting sensitive data and systems. You'll build the execution environments, orchestration, and controls that make this possible, and help enable the internal use of open-source models with appropriate protections around inference, tool use, and data access.

You'll work closely with the teams building Harvey's product sandbox and internal AI agent platform, shaping architecture and contributing production code to strengthen execution boundaries. Your impact will come from shipping systems, establishing a shared technical direction, and making security capabilities reusable across teams. You'll own work from design through rollout and operation, balancing containment with the reliability, performance, and flexibility that useful agents need.

What you'll do

  • Set the technical direction for secure agent execution, working across Security, Infrastructure, and Product Engineering to turn emerging capabilities and risks into a concrete roadmap.

  • Design, build, and operate a platform for security agents to discover and validate vulnerabilities within authorized targets and execution boundaries, producing reproducible evidence that engineers can act on.

  • Build reusable controls for agent tool use, code execution, network and filesystem access, resource consumption, and workload lifecycle. Integrate with identity and secrets platforms to limit access to the data and credentials each task needs.

  • Partner with the owners of Harvey's product sandbox and internal agent platform to make architectural decisions, implement protections, and integrate shared security capabilities into their execution environments.

  • Enable internal use of open-source models alongside infrastructure teams, building protections around model serving, agent execution, and sensitive-data handling.

  • Develop adversarial tests, evaluations, and telemetry that verify containment and expose failures. Build mechanisms to scope, observe, interrupt, and safely terminate agent activity.

  • Lead delivery and adoption across teams, mentor engineers, and remain hands-on through implementation and production operation, making clear tradeoffs across security, reliability, latency, and cost.

What You Have

  • 10+ years developing and running production software, including technical leadership on initiatives spanning multiple engineering teams.

  • Strong software engineering skills in languages such as Go, Rust, Python, or C++, with practical experience in Linux systems, networking, and containerized infrastructure.

  • Deep expertise in one or more areas of execution security, such as sandboxing, operating-system isolation, container or virtual-machine security, or platforms that execute untrusted code. You can translate threats into enforceable boundaries and test how those boundaries fail.

  • Experience building shared platforms, services, or libraries and helping other teams adopt them through clear interfaces, documentation, and safe migrations.

  • Experience with cloud infrastructure and distributed systems, including observability, failure handling, capacity management, and dependable production operation.

  • Fluency with AI-assisted engineering and agentic workflows: you use models to accelerate development, validate their output, and reason about the risks introduced when agents use tools, execute code, or access sensitive data.

  • Strong communication and technical judgment, with a record of bringing teams to agreement on ambiguous problems and carrying decisions through to delivery.

Nice to have

  • Experience with microVMs, hypervisors, or sandbox runtimes such as Firecracker, gVisor, or Kata Containers, or Linux isolation mechanisms such as namespaces, seccomp, and Landlock.

  • Experience building agent runtimes, tool-execution frameworks, or automated security-testing platforms.

  • Experience with vulnerability research, penetration testing, or adversarial evaluation of agent systems, including turning findings into reproducible tests and effective controls.

  • Experience deploying or securing self-hosted inference and open-source models, including isolation of model-serving workloads and protection of sensitive inputs and outputs.

Compensation

$231,000 - $346,400 USD

Role Overview

The Senior Technical Program Manager, GTM Technology leads delivery of cross-functional programs for Harvey's go-to-market systems. They join the program management team in Business Technology, Harvey's IT organization. This role ensures multi-team GTM technology programs are well planned, coordinated across teams, and delivered on time. They work with GTM systems and integrations teams to deliver programs for Sales, Marketing, Product, and Finance. It is an opportunity to deliver high-impact programs at an AI-native company as an early member of a growing program management team.

What You'll Do

  • Own end-to-end delivery of Business Technology's most strategic lead-to-cash programs, from planning through launch and retrospective.

  • Align cross-functional program teams on scope, sequencing, and milestones for programs that span CRM, marketing automation, sales engagement, and CPQ.

  • Coordinate delivery across Business Technology's GTM systems and integrations teams to keep programs on plan.

  • Surface risks, dependencies, and trade-offs early, and drive them to decisions with the right owners.

  • Give leadership clear visibility into program health through concise written updates, without adding overhead for delivery teams.

  • Contribute to shared, AI-enabled program practices that help the team deliver faster as Business Technology scales.

What You Have

  • 8+ years of experience in technical program management or a related role, with a track record of delivering complex, cross-functional GTM systems programs at high-growth B2B SaaS companies.

  • Experience leading at least one quote-to-cash, CRM, CPQ, or billing systems program end to end.

  • Working knowledge of GTM systems such as Salesforce and how they connect, enough to understand trade-offs and ask the right questions of systems teams.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders across Sales, Marketing, Product, and Finance without direct authority.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to distill complex programs into clear narratives for executive audiences.

  • Sound judgment on process and comfort with ambiguity. You right-size structure to the program and default to simple, AI-enabled ways of working.

Compensation

$150,000 - $205,000 USD

Harvey is looking for an experienced Executive Recruiter to support and scale our senior leadership hiring across functions and regions. Reporting to the Head of Executive Recruiting, you will partner closely with founders, executives, and VPs to attract and hire exceptional leadership talent from department heads to senior executives.

This role is highly visible and impactful, combining deep relationship building, rigorous research, and operational excellence. You will help deliver best in class executive hiring while contributing to the continued evolution of Harvey’s leadership recruiting strategy and processes.

What You'll Do

  • Own and drive end to end executive and senior leadership searches across the organization.

  • Contribute to scalable processes, tools, and metrics for executive hiring.

  • 6–10+ years of executive recruiting experience, ideally with a combination of search firm/agency and in house experience.
