We are looking for a Lead Technical Recruiter to help build Harvey Labs, our AI research organization.

You’ll partner closely with our Chief Research Officer and technical leadership to build the team from the ground up, initially focused on post-training talent across data and evaluations, infrastructure, and modeling and training. You’ll own searches end-to-end, develop talent strategies for highly specialized AI talent markets, and help define how we identify and attract exceptional technical talent as Harvey Labs scales.

This is a hands-on role with significant ownership. You’ll operate in ambiguity, develop a strong point of view on the AI talent landscape, and serve as a trusted advisor to technical leadership.

What You'll Do

  • Partner closely with our Chief Research Officer and Harvey Labs leadership to translate technical priorities into recruiting strategies

  • Own full-cycle recruiting across specialized AI/ML, research, and engineering roles

  • Build deep talent maps across leading AI companies, research labs, startups, academia, and open-source communities

  • Develop creative, high-touch sourcing and engagement strategies for exceptional talent, from experienced researchers to emerging new grads

  • Help leaders define new profiles, calibrate talent bars, and evolve search strategies based on market insights

  • Advise leadership on talent availability, competitive dynamics, compensation, and candidate motivations

  • Drive searches from initial market mapping through offer strategy, negotiation, and close

  • Use data and market intelligence to continuously improve our recruiting strategy

  • Help build scalable recruiting processes and raise the bar for technical recruiting across Harvey

What You Have

  • 7+ years of full-cycle technical recruiting experience in fast-paced, high-growth environments

  • Experience recruiting for technical AI research teams or similarly specialized technical roles

  • Strong aptitude for understanding complex technical domains and evaluating candidate qualifications

  • Exceptional sourcer who enjoys identifying hard-to-find talent across research labs, startups, academia, open source, and other nontraditional channels

  • Willing to take creative, white-glove approaches to engaging and closing exceptional talent

  • Trusted advisor who can build credibility with highly technical leaders and candidates

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and able to help shape searches when the profile isn't fully defined

  • Strong instincts for talent and a genuine interest in the evolving AI landscape

  • Data-driven and highly organized, with the ability to manage multiple complex searches without sacrificing candidate experience

  • High ownership, low ego, strong judgment, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves

  • Leads by example and helps elevate the broader recruiting team

  • Highly resourceful and fluent with modern AI tools, using them to accelerate research, sourcing, outreach, market mapping, and recruiting operations without sacrificing judgment or the candidate experience

Compensation

$163,900 - $245,900 USD

Role Overview

The People Operations Coordinator, Onboarding supports the operational foundation of Harvey's new hire experience, running the logistics, systems, and processes that make onboarding work end-to-end — from pre-arrival travel and scheduling through document collection, system processing, and in-person facilitation on day one.

This is a hands-on coordination role that sits at the center of a fast-growing People team, partnering daily with the People Operations team and cross-functionally with People Systems, Recruiting, Benefits, Payroll, and Legal. The onboarding program is scaling quickly and still being built in places, so this person will both execute a high volume of moving pieces with precision and help improve the systems and materials as the program matures. Success in the role means every new hire's first experience with Harvey feels welcoming, organized, and seamless.

What You'll Do

  • Facilitate in-person onboarding for New York–based new hire cohorts — run orientation and make sure every new hire feels welcomed and ready from day one.

  • Own onboarding logistics end-to-end: coordinate administrative filing and manage orientation schedules, decks, and calendar invites.

  • Process new hires accurately across our systems (Workday and related tools), with a clear eye on downstream impact to Payroll, Benefits, and IT.

  • Support pre-employment and compliance processes, including background checks, right-to-work verification, and required document collection and filing across our global regions.

  • Support the creation and maintenance onboarding materials — orientation slides, onboarding guides, and internal documentation — keeping content accurate as the program evolves.

  • Manage new hire communications, support onboarding automations (email sequences and calendar workflows), and surface field feedback to help improve the program at scale.

What You Have

  • 1–3+ years in HR, People Operations, onboarding, event management, or a related operations or coordination role.

  • Experience with an HRIS (Workday strongly preferred); familiarity with onboarding workflows a plus.

  • High attention to detail and strong follow-through — you catch your own errors and close loops without being reminded.

  • Flexibility and composure in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment — you adjust quickly when priorities shift and manage multiple competing tasks without dropping the ball.

  • Strong communication and facilitation skills — you keep new hires informed, flag issues proactively, and can confidently own a room in front of a large cohort.

  • Comfort with global context: multi-country document requirements, regional compliance differences, and coordinating calendars across time zones.

Nice to have: prior experience at a startup or high-growth company; exposure to global HR operations or multi-entity environments; a track record of presenting or facilitating deck-based content with energy and clarity.

$81,200 - $121,800 USD

 - Process new hires accurately across our systems (Workday and related tools), with a clear eye on downstream impact to Payroll, Benefits, and IT.

 - Support pre-employment and compliance processes, including background checks, right-to-work verification, and required document collection and filing across our global regions.

 - Support the creation and maintenance onboarding materials — orientation slides, onboarding guides, and internal documentation — keeping content accurate as the program evolves.

 - Manage new hire communications, support onboarding automations (email sequences and calendar workflows), and surface field feedback to help improve the program at scale.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Experience with an HRIS (Workday strongly preferred); familiarity with onboarding workflows a plus.

 - High attention to detail and strong follow-through — you catch your own errors and close loops without being reminded.

 - Flexibility and composure in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment — you adjust quickly when priorities shift and manage multiple competing tasks without dropping the ball.

 - Strong communication and facilitation skills — you keep new hires informed, flag issues proactively, and can confidently own a room in front of a large cohort.

 - Comfort with global context: multi-country document requirements, regional compliance differences, and coordinating calendars across time zones.

Nice to have: prior experience at a startup or high-growth company; exposure to global HR operations or multi-entity environments; a track record of presenting or facilitating deck-based content with energy and clarity.

$81,200 - $121,800 USD

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

As a Software Engineer, Intern (Summer 2027) on the Engineering team at Harvey, you’ll work alongside experienced engineers on projects that power our AI products. You’ll collaborate with our Product, AI, Legal, and GTM teams to help build secure, intuitive systems that deliver real value to our customers.

This 12 or 16 week internship is ideal for students who are curious, motivated, and excited to learn how modern application-layer and GenAI products are built. You’ll gain hands-on experience across the stack, contribute to real features, and see how your work impacts users in production.

We're currently hiring Winter 2027 interns in Toronto and Summer 2027 interns in New York and San Francisco across multiple teams and roles, including Frontend, Backend, Full-Stack, Infrastructure, and Applied AI intern roles. Your interests & experience will be factored into our team matching process, where you’ll have the opportunity to learn about teams across Harvey including Agents, Applied AI, Assistant, Enterprise, Infrastructure, Mobile, Vault and many others.

What You'll Do

You will:

  • Own a project end-to-end from coding and testing to deploying it to production, and presenting your work to peers and leaders across the company.

  • Write clean, maintainable code that meets our team's standards. You'll use AI-assisted development tools daily, and you’ll own the quality of everything you ship—AI-generated or not.

  • Build real knowledge of the systems you support and the users they serve, bringing that perspective into product discussions.

  • Debug problems in your area, follow escalation procedures, and treat quality as urgent. Our users are lawyers doing high-stakes work.

  • Collaborate with your team through code review, pair programming, design reviews and technical documentation.

  • Depending on your team, you could work on retrieval over large document collections, interfaces for collaborating with AI systems, multi-region compute infrastructure, enterprise agents, or secure systems for sensitive client data. You'll also evaluate frontier models alongside senior engineers.

What You Have

  • Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program in computer science, engineering, or a related field with a graduation date of December 2027 or later.

  • Able to work from our New York or San Francisco offices during our summer cohort, based on your academic schedule. Relocation support is available.

  • Previous internship experience is required.

  • Technical foundation. Strong proficiency in one or more languages (Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Java, Go, or similar) and solid general computer science knowledge.

  • Decisiveness. You have a bias toward action. You've built something start to finish in coursework, a personal project, or in a past internship, and you know the difference between a decision you should make yourself and one worth getting feedback on. You'd rather move and correct course than stall.

  • Simplicity. You can explain a complex technical idea in plain language, whether or not the person you're explaining it to is an engineer. You look for the simplest solution that works, and you know when added complexity is worth it.

  • Job's Not Finished. You aren't satisfied when something merely works. You proactively seek out feedback, act on it, and keep pushing after the assignment is technically complete. Internship experience specifically at an early-stage startup is a plus.

  • AI Forward. Comfortable using AI-assisted development tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) and curious about building LLMs into your own coding workflow.

Our interview process includes AI-assisted coding sessions; you'll be expected to work with AI tools the way you would on the job.

Compensation

  • Pay: $62/hr-$72/hr in San Francisco and New York

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We are looking for a Lead Technical Recruiter to help build Harvey Labs, our AI research organization.

You’ll partner closely with our Chief Research Officer and technical leadership to build the team from the ground up, initially focused on post-training talent across data and evaluations, infrastructure, and modeling and training. You’ll own searches end-to-end, develop talent strategies for highly specialized AI talent markets, and help define how we identify and attract exceptional technical talent as Harvey Labs scales.

This is a hands-on role with significant ownership. You’ll operate in ambiguity, develop a strong point of view on the AI talent landscape, and serve as a trusted advisor to technical leadership.

What You'll Do

  • Partner closely with our Chief Research Officer and Harvey Labs leadership to translate technical priorities into recruiting strategies

  • Own full-cycle recruiting across specialized AI/ML, research, and engineering roles

  • Build deep talent maps across leading AI companies, research labs, startups, academia, and open-source communities

  • Develop creative, high-touch sourcing and engagement strategies for exceptional talent, from experienced researchers to emerging new grads

  • Help leaders define new profiles, calibrate talent bars, and evolve search strategies based on market insights

  • Advise leadership on talent availability, competitive dynamics, compensation, and candidate motivations

  • Drive searches from initial market mapping through offer strategy, negotiation, and close

  • Use data and market intelligence to continuously improve our recruiting strategy

  • Help build scalable recruiting processes and raise the bar for technical recruiting across Harvey

What You Have

  • 7+ years of full-cycle technical recruiting experience in fast-paced, high-growth environments

  • Experience recruiting for technical AI research teams or similarly specialized technical roles

  • Strong aptitude for understanding complex technical domains and evaluating candidate qualifications

  • Exceptional sourcer who enjoys identifying hard-to-find talent across research labs, startups, academia, open source, and other nontraditional channels

  • Willing to take creative, white-glove approaches to engaging and closing exceptional talent

  • Trusted advisor who can build credibility with highly technical leaders and candidates

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and able to help shape searches when the profile isn't fully defined

  • Strong instincts for talent and a genuine interest in the evolving AI landscape

  • Data-driven and highly organized, with the ability to manage multiple complex searches without sacrificing candidate experience

  • High ownership, low ego, strong judgment, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves

  • Leads by example and helps elevate the broader recruiting team

  • Highly resourceful and fluent with modern AI tools, using them to accelerate research, sourcing, outreach, market mapping, and recruiting operations without sacrificing judgment or the candidate experience

Compensation

$163,900 - $245,900 USD

Role Overview

As a Customer Success Manager you’ll play a critical role in guiding our clients through their journey with Harvey, and help define the future of work at both law firms and in-house teams. This position is pivotal in ensuring our clients not only adopt but also derive maximum value from our technology. You'll act as a trusted advisor, deeply integrating Harvey into their business processes and workflows. This individual will also have a chance to design and deploy scalable 1:many solutions that will impact how we serve our broad mid-market customer base in a highly efficient manner at scale.

What You'll Do

  • Strategic Implementation: Lead the integration of Harvey into client workflows, ensuring seamless adoption and optimal use of our AI solutions.

  • Training & Enablement: Evangelize the power of LLMs as you meet with and enable end users to adopt Harvey on a daily-basis as it becomes a “must have” product.

  • Client Relationship Management: Serve as the primary contact for 40+ mid-market clients with a prescriptive and consultative approach and delivering a superior customer experience.

  • Process Creation: Drive scalability in the way we operate through documentation, designing playbooks, self-help materials, email cadences, and automation to ensure we drive efficiency in our long term mid-market strategy.

  • Success Metrics Management: Utilize adoption rates, benchmarks, and other key metrics to drive strategies ensuring client satisfaction and high ROI.

  • Advocacy and Engagement: Encourage user and stakeholder engagement, transforming them into Harvey advocates within their organizations.

  • Customer Health Monitoring: Use analytics and feedback to maintain customer satisfaction, ensuring readiness for renewal and expansion opportunities.

  • Feedback Loop: Relay client insights back to our internal teams, aiding in the continuous improvement of our product and services.

What You Have

  • Experienced professionals from legal firms or SaaS organizations, with direct experience managing a high volume of client cases and/or customers.

  • Individuals with excellent communication and strategic planning skills, capable of influencing stakeholders at various levels.

  • Results driven candidates who are able to ruthlessly prioritize competing tasks and demanding customers seamlessly.

  • Team players described as empathetic, committed, structured, motivated, and collaborative with a team-first mentality.

  • Experience with Salesforce and Catalyst, are preferred, but not required.

What We Offer

  • A chance to be at the forefront of AI technology and innovation, directly impacting how our clients' businesses operate and thrive.

  • An opportunity to contribute to the growth and direction of our Customer Success program, building out best-in-class playbooks and processes.

  • A collaborative work environment that promotes growth, learning, and development.

Compensation Range

$125,000 - $145,000 OTE

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey is building a best-in-class go-to-market engine, and we're looking for a Lead System Administrator, CX is a senior individual contributor responsible for administering, operating, and continuously improving Harvey's Zendesk platform and the broader Customer Experience systems stack, including Planhat, Sierra, and new platforms as they are adopted, across the full customer journey from pilot through renewal. Zendesk is the primary system of ownership; the stack around it is growing, and this role grows with it.

This role applies deep platform expertise to design scalable workflows, implement automation, and maintain system reliability so Zendesk and its integrations evolve alongside the business while maintaining strong governance, documentation, and stability. You'll balance hands-on configuration with operational improvement and serve as the primary systems partner to Customer Support and CX Operations leadership.

The role sits within GTM Systems and partners closely with CX Operations, Support, Customer Success, Integrations, and Data teams. Success requires strong technical judgment, operational ownership, and the ability to independently translate operational requirements into scalable, reliable system configurations.

What You'll Do

Own Zendesk

  • Administer Support, Guide, Explore, and AI features, and act as the internal Zendesk subject matter expert.

  • Design and maintain scalable workflows: routing, triggers, automations, forms and fields, taxonomy, SLAs, views, macros, and queues.

  • Manage the configuration lifecycle (planning, sandbox testing, deployment, documentation) with strong governance and traceability.

  • Manage vendor releases and platform changes, including the upcoming OAuth migration.

  • Troubleshoot complex issues across workflows and integrations, and drive root-cause resolution.

  • Build Explore dashboards and support the data pipeline behind executive reporting on support performance and customer health.

Grow the CX stack

  • Support and optimize adjacent CX and CS platforms, including Planhat for customer health, lifecycle, and renewal workflows and Sierra for AI-assisted support, as CX priorities require.

  • Evaluate, implement, and administer new CX platforms as the stack expands, applying the same configuration lifecycle, governance, and documentation standards used for Zendesk.

  • Work with Integrations, Data, and Security to connect systems in line with Harvey's security and compliance standards.

Run the function

  • Manage intake and prioritization of enhancement requests and maintain a clear backlog.

  • Lead enhancement projects: define requirements and acceptance criteria, coordinate stakeholders, and communicate scope, risks, and schedule changes proactively.

  • Meet operational SLAs for platform support and configuration requests.

  • Join CX Operations planning and agent feedback forums, and work with agents on QA and user acceptance testing.

  • Provide training and enablement when needed, and maintain system design documentation.

  • Ship changes that are designed, tested, documented, and communicated, and bring firm recommendations with trade-offs rather than just problems.

What You Have

  • 5+ years administering Zendesk in a high-volume, multi-team environment, with deep expertise in triggers, automations, routing, fields, forms, views, macros, and SLAs

  • Zendesk Administrator certification (Support Admin Expert or equivalent)

  • Experience with sandbox testing, controlled deployment, and change documentation

  • Experience building Zendesk integrations with CRM or adjacent systems via iPaaS (Workato preferred), APIs, or webhooks

  • Working knowledge of Salesforce as an integration partner (objects, field mapping, sync patterns)

  • Experience building reporting and dashboards in Zendesk Explore or a similar tool

  • Experience with Planhat, Gainsight, Catalyst, or similar, or a demonstrated ability to ramp quickly on new CX tools

  • Strong documentation habits, including runbooks and change records

  • Ability to translate operational workflows into scalable configurations and communicate with technical and non-technical partners

  • Ability to manage multiple initiatives independently

  • Fluency with AI tools (including Zendesk AI and general-purpose assistants) to build, automate, and troubleshoot

Bonus

  • Experience administering additional Zendesk products (Talk, Workforce Management, Advanced AI).

  • Experience integrating AI support agents (Sierra or similar) with Zendesk.

  • SQL or scripting for data workflows; Snowflake or BigQuery.

  • Experience in compliance-driven environments (SOC 2, etc.).

Compensation

$171,000 - $235,200 USD

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We’re looking for a hands-on Field Marketing Manager to help scale Harvey’s EMEA field marketing motion as it grows from early foundations into a repeatable, region-wide programme.

The groundwork is underway: playbooks, agency relationships, event criteria, and reporting. Your job is to take them further. You’ll join a small EMEA field team, own a significant share of the event programme, and help transform our field motion across every market in EMEA.

You’ll own both first-party and third-party field events, from executive dinners and roundtables to conferences and sponsorships. The role is highly executional, but also highly strategic: you’ll be expected to get deep into the details while helping define what “great” looks like for field marketing at Harvey.

This is a role for someone who loves being close to the action: partnering with Sales, working events on the ground, improving every touchpoint, and turning a high-volume motion into a repeatable, measurable, high-quality growth engine.

What You'll Do

  • Scale the EMEA field marketing engine: build on the existing playbooks, processes, planning rhythms, agency model, vendor bench, and measurement foundations, and strengthen them so field marketing can run at higher volume across more markets without losing quality.

  • Plan and execute high-quality field programmes: own a portfolio of third-party conferences and first-party events (executive dinners, roundtables, and hosted formats) end to end, from selection and planning through to onsite delivery and follow-up.

  • Partner deeply with GTM: work with Sales and customer-facing teams to prioritise markets, accounts, audiences, and event formats that support pipeline generation, opportunity acceleration, and strategic relationship building.

  • Raise the quality bar for how Harvey shows up: booth experiences, onsite execution, pre-event targeting, attendee briefing, Sales enablement, VIP moments, follow-up, and post-event reporting.

  • Make event motions scalable: apply and sharpen the frameworks for when we sponsor, when we host, what package we buy, who attends, what Sales needs to do, and how success is measured, so each new event is faster to stand up than the last.

  • Own execution details: manage budgets, logistics, vendors, agencies, timelines, staffing, swag, onsite delivery, lead capture, and follow-up across multiple events and markets.

  • Measure and improve impact: track performance across field activity and feed what you learn back into the shared EMEA field plan.


What You Have

  • 4–7 years of experience in field marketing or event marketing, ideally in B2B SaaS, technology, or professional services, including experience scaling a motion rather than only running an established one.

  • Proven experience planning and executing high-quality events or field activations that support pipeline, lead generation, account engagement, or revenue impact.

  • Strong Sales partnership instincts and experience.

  • Comfortable working autonomously in a fast-paced environment.

  • Highly organised and operationally rigorous, with a high bar for detail and the ability to manage multiple events, stakeholders, vendors, and timelines at once.

  • Comfortable taking early-stage processes and making them stronger and more efficient.

  • Strong commercial judgement, with the ability to connect event activity to GTM priorities and measurable business outcomes.

  • Comfortable getting hands-on, from strategy and planning through to onsite execution, rep wrangling, logistics, and follow-up.

  • Familiarity with AI tooling is highly desirable.

  • Experience marketing to legal, financial services, consulting, enterprise, or other high-touch professional audiences is a plus.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

You run the building and the operational systems behind the New York office. You are the subject-matter expert on how the space works, who to call, what the building requires, how our vendors are performing, and what the operational data is telling us.

This is a senior individual-contributor role, not a people-manager role. “Senior” reflects the complexity, judgment, and independence of your scope. The Coordinator owns office experience/programs and general office execution; the Assistant owns the front desk. You own building operations, facilities, vendors, and the systems/data that let the Manager make good decisions.

What You'll Do

  • Conduct regular walkthroughs of the office to proactively identify facilities, maintenance, F&B, service, safety, and space-readiness issues before they become employee problems.

  • Hold the day-to-day property-management relationship and own building work orders through resolution.

  • Own facilities issues including HVAC/temperature, plumbing, lighting/electrical, leaks, doors, appliances, physical repairs, and preventative maintenance.

  • Diagnose and route issues to the right building/vendor partner, follow through, and verify the fix actually held.

  • Manage freight/loading-dock logistics and other building-specific operating requirements.

  • Communicate directly with employees when building/facilities work affects the office; office-wide communications are reviewed by the Workplace Manager except for highly tactical, time-sensitive updates.

What You Have

  • 4+ years in workplace operations, office management, facilities, or hospitality with meaningful facilities/vendor responsibility.

  • Direct experience managing vendors and contractors and holding them to scope.

  • Working understanding of HVAC, plumbing, electrical/lighting, and commercial-building operations.

  • Familiarity with work orders, COIs, property management, and preventative maintenance.

  • Strong operational judgment and ability to distinguish an isolated issue from a pattern requiring escalation.

  • Comfort with operational data, spend tracking, and turning day-to-day information into useful insights.

  • Bias toward walking the floor and finding problems before tickets do.

  • Clear, direct communication and willingness to communicate about work within your lane.

  • Experience with an office relocation/opening is a strong plus.

Compensation

$110,000 - $150,000 USD

The AE will own the full sales cycle for a defined portfolio of public sector accounts, partnering with legal engineers, solutions architects, and product teams to deliver tailored outcomes in a highly regulated buying environment. It is a rare opportunity to shape a high-impact vertical in one of Harvey's fastest-growing international markets, working at the intersection of AI and public sector legal and policy workflows.

What You'll Do

  • Own and grow a portfolio of named public sector enterprise accounts across ANZ, driving full-funnel sales activity from prospecting through commercial negotiation, contracting, and onboarding.

  • Develop a deep understanding of public sector procurement processes, compliance requirements, and decision-making structures to position Harvey's AI platform effectively.

  • Lead high-impact product demonstrations and client engagements that articulate Harvey's value to government stakeholders, legal counsel, and senior executives.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with product, legal engineering, solutions architecture, and GTM teams to inform roadmap priorities and surface client needs.

  • Build and maintain long-term relationships with key decision-makers across public sector institutions, driving expansion and retention within accounts.

  • Document learnings, refine messaging, and contribute to scalable playbooks that support Harvey's broader public sector go-to-market strategy in the region.

What You Have

  • Experience in enterprise B2B SaaS sales, with a strong preference for experience selling into government or public sector accounts.

  • Proven ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles with long procurement timelines and regulatory requirements.

  • Familiarity with public sector procurement in Australia and/or New Zealand, including panel arrangements, tender processes, and compliance frameworks.

  • Interest in the legal industry and a commitment to advancing knowledge work through technology.

  • Self-motivated and results-oriented, with a collaborative approach to working across functions in a high-growth environment.

This is a full-stack regional marketing leadership role. You own the marketing plan for APAC end to end: demand generation, field marketing and events, and the localization of Harvey's product and segment narratives for the region's distinct markets. You will manage a small existing team and be in charge of growing it rapidly across markets. You will serve as the partner to Harvey’s regional sales and customer success leaders, partner closely with Harvey's global marketing functions, and operate with a high degree of autonomy and ownership.

What you'll do

  • Own the APAC marketing strategy and quarterly plans: define priority markets, segments, and audiences; set regional targets; and allocate budget across demand generation, field, brand, and content.

  • Carry a regional pipeline number. Build, measure, and report on the programs that generate, influence, and accelerate pipeline across APAC, in tight partnership with regional Sales and Customer Success leadership.

  • Lead and develop the APAC marketing team, hiring against a growing plan and building the regional structure, rituals, and operating cadence as the team scales.

  • Own the regional event and field portfolio with clear prioritization criteria, measurement, and follow-through with GTM.

  • Adapt Harvey's global positioning and product narratives for APAC audiences, working with Product Marketing to reflect regional realities including data residency and sovereignty requirements, regulatory expectations, and market-specific buying dynamics.

  • Build Harvey's brand and voice in the region: partner with comms on media relationships, develop customer references and stories, build executive thought leadership, and the local legal and professional services community.

  • Run regional demand generation in partnership with the global Demand Gen team — campaigns, paid media, lifecycle, and web localization — with disciplined attribution and reporting.

  • Act as the voice of the APAC market inside Harvey, bringing customer, competitive, and regulatory insight back to Product, Product Marketing, and executive leadership to shape the roadmap and global strategy.

What you have

  • 10+ years in B2B marketing with meaningful time leading marketing across multiple APAC markets, ideally in enterprise SaaS, AI, or professional services.

  • A track record of owning a regional number: demonstrable pipeline and revenue impact from programs you built, not just campaigns you ran.

  • Genuine full-stack range. You have owned demand generation and field marketing, and you can also hold your own on brand, messaging, and communications.

  • Experience managing and growing a distributed team, including hiring in more than one APAC market.

  • Nuanced understanding of how key APAC markets like Australia, Singapore, Japan and Korea differ and a point of view on how those differences should shape programming and sequencing.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the judgment to know when global assets work as-is and when a market needs something built for it.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-growing environment with ambiguity, cross-functional complexity, and a high degree of ownership.

Additional Information

  • Location: Sydney, NSW (Hybrid with flexibility)

  • Work eligibility: Must have valid Australian work rights; Harvey does not currently offer visa sponsorship for this role

What We Offer

  • Structured hybrid working arrangement: 3 days in our Sydney office, 2 days working from home

  • Health Coverage: Fully covered private hospital insurance, plus extras for dental, optical, physio, mental health, and more.

  • Family & Fertility Support: Support for fertility treatments, adoption, and surrogacy through Carrot.

  • Retirement & Security: Comprehensive coverage designed to support your long-term well-being.

  • Paid Leave: Paid annual leave, sick leave, and fully paid parental leave for all parents.

  • Wellness & Perks: Daily in-office lunch, wellness memberships through Wellhub, and monthly commuting support.

  • Professional Development: Annual support for courses, certifications, conferences, and books.

  • Remote Work Allowance: Monthly support for home office, internet, and phone expenses.

  • Harvey Holiday: After four years, enjoy a four-week paid sabbatical to rest, travel, or explore new experiences.

We are still early. That means you will operate across altitudes, setting strategy, building structure, and staying close to the field on critical deals. You will help define how Harvey shows up in the North America market, shape our sales motion, and ensure we are delivering real value to customers adopting AI in high-stakes competitive environments.

We are looking for someone who has led multi-team segments, developed high-potential sales managers, scaled teams in ambiguity, and knows what great looks like in complex SaaS sales.

What You'll Do

  • Lead, coach and develop a team of SMB Sales Managers across North America, driving accountability for net new logo targets.

  • Implement and maintain a rigorous sales operating cadence, including seller onboarding, enablement, coaching, pipeline generation, and deal execution

  • Drive the regional sales strategy, including territory design, coverage models, and go-to-market execution.

  • Own North America SMB forecasting and pipeline health, providing accurate reporting to senior leadership.

  • Hire, coach, and retain top managerial talent; build a strong leadership bench across the region.

  • Partner with global SMB leadership to localize and refine the sales playbook for North America markets.

  • Develop executive relationships with Harvey’s highest value SMB customers across the region

  • Work cross-functionally with marketing, solutions engineering, legal, and customer success to ensure a cohesive customer experience across the region.

  • Represent North America SMB in global planning cycles, headcount discussions, and strategic initiatives.

What You Have

  • 10+ years of B2B tech sales experience, including 4+ years managing and developing sales managers or senior individual contributors.

  • Demonstrated success leading a regional or multi-market sales organization in a high-growth, early-stage environment.

  • Strong track record of selling complex software to enterprise or SMB clients using a consultative, value-based methodology.

  • Experience operating across North America markets, with an understanding of regional dynamics, buyer behaviors, and legal industry nuances.

  • Exceptional communication and executive presence — able to influence both frontline teams and senior stakeholders.

  • Genuine passion for Harvey's mission and a strong interest in how AI is transforming knowledge work and the legal profession.

Compensation

$340,000 USD OTE 50/50

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey's users are among the most sophisticated professionals - from managing partners and practice leaders at global law firms to GCs and legal operations executives in-house, and tax and finance leaders adopting AI across their organizations.

These professionals are navigating a fundamental shift in how their work gets done. Reaching them starts with deeply understanding the realities of that work: the problems worth solving, the outcomes that matter, and the questions and skepticism that come with adopting AI. Our best campaigns turn that understanding into ideas and experiences that are useful, credible, and relevant to where each audience is on that journey.

The Senior Integrated Campaigns Manager will build the function responsible for doing exactly that.

You'll drive Harvey's global integrated campaign from strategy to execution: defining our priority audiences, sharpening how we position Harvey, and designing coordinated programs that build awareness, deepen engagement, and drive growth. This is a strategic and high impact role with meaningful influence across the company.

What You'll Do

  • Set Harvey's global integrated campaign strategy. Define the audiences, segments, narratives, and campaign architecture that build relevance with our audiences and drive awareness, engagement, pipeline, and revenue.

  • Turn audience insight into differentiated positioning. Develop messaging rooted in primary research, customer insight, competitive intelligence, and demonstrated use cases. Build claims on evidence and create narratives sophisticated audiences find credible.

  • Translate company priorities into market-facing programs. Partner with Product, Sales, and business leaders to develop marketing strategies around Harvey's most important growth initiatives, connecting what matters to the business with what matters to our audiences.

  • Orchestrate the full marketing system. Bring together digital, social, communications and analyst relations, alliances, events, field marketing, and other channels into cohesive global campaigns, spanning major launches, category-building moments, and always-on programs.

  • Analytics and optimization. Track and report key campaign goals, performance metrics, and operating cadence that connect campaign investment to audience and business outcomes.

  • Raise the creative and strategic bar. Establish what great campaign thinking looks like at Harvey, from the quality of the insight and sharpness of the message to the craft of the execution and rigor of the measurement.

  • Build an AI-native campaign engine. Apply AI across audience research and modeling, creative development, experimentation, personalization, localization, and performance analysis. Develop repeatable approaches that raise the capabilities of the broader marketing organization.

What You Have

  • 5+ years of B2B marketing experience, including significant ownership of integrated campaigns, demand generation, or go-to-market programs within enterprise software or high-growth SaaS.

  • Strong commercial instincts. You've owned multi-million-dollar investments and understand how to connect marketing decisions to audience impact, pipeline, revenue, and ROI.

  • Exceptional positioning and messaging judgment. You know how to get from audience research and market insight to a differentiated point of view, and you're a strong enough writer to do the work yourself when the stakes are high.

  • Exceptional cross-functional influence. You've orchestrated digital, social, communications, analyst relations, partnerships, events, and field marketing as one system rather than optimizing a single channel in isolation.

  • Hands-on fluency with AI. AI is already part of your campaign workflow. You have informed opinions about where it meaningfully improves marketing, and where human judgment remains the advantage.

  • Comfort with ambition and ambiguity. You can create clarity where there isn't yet a playbook, move quickly without lowering the bar, and build systems that become more sophisticated as Harvey grows.

Compensation

$136,000 - $187,000 USD

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey’s Legal Engineers are skilled lawyers from top-tier law firms who apply their legal experience to ensure that current and prospective customers understand how Harvey’s solutions enhance specific day-to-day workflows, working alongside Harvey’s Account Executives to support all aspects of our sales strategy. Legal Engineers build consultative relationships with law firm partners and associates and in-house attorneys at private equity firms and Fortune 500 companies, becoming trusted advisors on how Harvey’s AI solutions can make them more effective.

Similar to how Solutions Architects secure the “technical win” in the sales process, Legal Engineers secure the “legal win” by performing in-depth customer discovery and education on Harvey’s solutions through targeted meetings and demos that resonate with the customer’s day-to-day workflows specific to their legal practice area.

Legal Engineers utilize their experience practicing law and their legal mindset to ask thoughtful questions to understand the needs of law firm and in-house attorneys, develop credibility, and then partner with Account Executives to educate them on Harvey’s value via large and small group sessions as well as one-to-one conversations.

What You'll Do

  • Engage with English- and Swedish-speaking lawyers at existing and prospective customers to understand their workflow challenges, strategic objectives, and broader firm context — then demonstrate how Harvey’s AI solutions can address them.

  • Establish yourself as a credible expert in solving customers’ specific legal problems (e.g. researching public and private databases for certain types of information, drafting and analyzing contractual provisions and whole documents, analyzing briefs and filings, corporate governance, conducting due diligence).

  • Lead product demonstrations tailored to the context of various law firm practice groups and in-house legal teams, asking questions to validate how Harvey can add value and then showcasing Harvey’s features and benefits relevant to each prospective client’s potential use cases.

  • Partner with the marketing team to develop content that will resonate with lawyers, tailored to the unique needs of their practice areas and client types.

  • Act as the “Voice of the Customer,” using your legal perspective to help the broader sales team to develop and implement more effective strategies and synthesize customer feedback for the product team through a legal lens.

  • Tailor the introduction of new solutions to specific customer needs.

  • Further the market perception of Harvey as uniquely credible, substantive, and helpful in applying its AI solutions to make lawyers better at their jobs.

  • Conduct research and analysis on customers and competitors.

What You Have

  • JD or equivalent legal qualification.

  • Fluent in Swedish and English.

  • At least 3 years of experience practicing law at a top-tier law firm, preferably with a corporate or litigation focus.

  • Executive engagement skills and presence, with an ability to establish strong relationships with key decision makers and build credibility at all levels.

  • Outstanding presentation skills to both legal and executive audiences, whether impromptu on a whiteboard or using presentations and demos.

  • Strong understanding of legal processes and challenges faced by legal professionals.

  • Curiosity about AI’s potential to transform the legal industry.

  • Sales or customer-facing experience, including law firm business development and/or secondment, is a plus, as is experience directly managing law firm client matters and client relationships.

Additional Information

  • Location: Sweden

  • Work eligibility: Must have valid Swedish work rights; Harvey does not currently offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices [here].

You will act as a trusted thought partner to APAC Sales Leadership and cross-functional stakeholders, helping connect regional realities to Harvey’s global go-to-market model. It’s a chance to build and scale a high-impact function in a fast-growing, category-defining AI company.

What You’ll Do

  • Partner with APAC Enterprise Sales Leadership to define field strategy for APAC and ensure alignment with Harvey’s global GTM operating model, enabling predictable, durable revenue growth across the region.

  • Drive forecast rigor and pipeline quality by establishing clear expectations, processes, and inspection mechanisms that improve CRM hygiene, data accuracy, and visibility into risk and upside.

  • Design, implement, and evolve regional operating rhythms (business reviews, forecast calls, pipeline reviews, planning cadences) that support disciplined execution and scale as the business grows.

  • Lead high-priority GTM initiatives for APAC that tackle complex, cross-functional problems (e.g., territory and coverage design, segmentation, capacity and headcount modeling, market-entry playbooks) and translate them into clear plans for the field.

  • Partner closely with GTM Enablement to identify capability gaps, shape regional enablement priorities, and support the onboarding and ramp of new AEs and SDRs through data-driven insights and feedback loops.

  • Over time, build and develop a high-performing team of APAC Sales Business Partners, setting a high bar on analytical rigor, stakeholder partnership, and operational excellence.

  • Serve as the connective tissue between APAC and global Revenue Operations, sharing learnings, advocating for regional needs, and helping standardize best practices across markets where it makes sense.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Strategy & Operations, or a closely related field.

  • Experience in high-growth technology environments combined with backgrounds in investment banking, private equity, venture capital, strategy/management consulting, or similarly analytical roles is strongly preferred.

  • 2+ years of people management experience leading high-performing, analytically oriented teams.

  • Demonstrated track record as a strategic business partner to senior GTM leaders, with the ability to build trust, navigate diverse working styles, and influence cross-functional stakeholders without direct authority.

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills; you are energized by working across Sales, CS, Marketing, Finance, Product, and Enablement to drive toward shared commercial outcomes.

  • Comfort operating in fast-paced, highly ambiguous environments, with a bias toward structured thinking, clear communication, and high-quality execution under time pressure. .

Additional Information

  • Location: Singapore, NSW (Hybrid with flexibility)

  • Work eligibility: Must have valid Australian work rights; Harvey does not currently offer visa sponsorship for this role

What We Offer

  • Structured hybrid working arrangement: 3 days in our Sydney office, 2 days working from home

  • Health Coverage: Fully covered private hospital insurance, plus extras for dental, optical, physio, mental health, and more.

  • Family & Fertility Support: Support for fertility treatments, adoption, and surrogacy through Carrot.

  • Retirement & Security: Comprehensive coverage designed to support your long-term well-being.

  • Paid Leave: Paid annual leave, sick leave, and fully paid parental leave for all parents.

  • Wellness & Perks: Daily in-office lunch, wellness memberships through Wellhub, and monthly commuting support.

  • Professional Development: Annual support for courses, certifications, conferences, and books.

  • Remote Work Allowance: Monthly support for home office, internet, and phone expenses.

  • Harvey Holiday: After four years, enjoy a four-week paid sabbatical to rest, travel, or explore new experiences.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey is looking for a Customer Experience (CX) Manager to lead a high-performing support team serving lawyers and professional services teams. Our customers hold their own work to a high standard of accuracy and timeliness, and expect the same from our support. How well your region runs is one of the biggest levers Harvey has on what customers actually experience when they need help. Reporting to the Head of CX, you'll drive operational excellence and accountability across Harvey's global support organization.

You'll balance strategic oversight with hands-on execution. This is a role for a leader who thrives in motion: proactive, decisive, and deeply motivated by achieving results through your team. You'll inherit a metric set and processes that need to be better, and we expect you to diagnose what's broken and fix it without being asked.

You'll also be one of five CX Managers across the globe, and that peer group is where our operating standard gets set. You're expected to trade what's working across regions and push for the changes you think we should make everywhere, shaping the culture and cadence of a growing support organization.

What You'll Do

  • Run day-to-day support delivery for your region: queue and coverage, triage and handoff, and escalation judgment, measured by First Response Time, Resolution Time, QA, and cSAT. When a number moves, you find the root cause and fix it or scale it.

  • Set individual performance expectations and stay close enough to the work to spot drift early. Coach against QA results in the moment, and move to a documented plan only when coaching hasn't landed.

  • Own escalations end to end: triage and severity judgment, customer communication through to resolution, and bug reports Engineering can act on without a follow-up thread. Partner with Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market to turn recurring escalations into fixes.

  • Take part in the on-call rotation for customer-impacting incidents, owning the coordination of response and customer communication strategy while an incident is live.

  • Drive adoption of the AI tools and systems we provide across triage, drafting, deflection, and QA, and pressure-test what CX Ops ships against real queue conditions.

  • Track how your region performs against the other four, bring what's working to your peers, adopt what's working in theirs, and propose the practices you think should apply globally.

  • Forecast coverage and staffing against volume, and flag gaps before they have impact.

  • Hire, onboard, and develop team members to ensure readiness for future growth and evolving support needs

What You Have

  • 10+ years in customer support or customer experience, including 4+ years managing teams in a high-volume environment serving enterprise customers.

  • Comfortable operating at Harvey's pace, not a typical enterprise pace. This is consistently the hardest bar for otherwise-strong support managers to clear.

  • A deep focus on the customer, and real satisfaction in solving the problems that make their work harder than it needs to be.

  • You are genuinely invested in developing your team, and you know a high bar is part of that.

  • You manage close to the work. You know what your team's tickets actually look like, not just what the dashboard says.

  • A change you made to how a support team works that produced a step change, not an incremental gain. You saw the leverage point others in the seat missed.

  • Ownership of a metric set (FRT, TTR, cSAT, QA, backlog, deflection): what drives each one, what to change when one slips, and the ability to build your own reporting. We use Zendesk, Salesforce, Omni, and Snowflake.

  • You understand enterprise escalations, from severity judgment through the customer conversation, and can work one yourself: reproduce the issue, read error logs, and troubleshoot API, authentication, and AI output quality issues well enough to brief Engineering accurately.

  • You can take a process improvement from idea to shipped yourself, and you know which ones to handover to someone on your team instead.

  • Day-to-day proficiency using AI tools in a production support workflow, not experimentation, and a concrete point of view on how AI is changing what a support team should look like.

  • Admin-level fluency with Zendesk or an equivalent platform: views, triggers, macros, and routing logic.

Additional Information

  • Work eligibility: Must be authorized to work in India. Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

  • Achieve and exceed revenue targets and other key sales metrics.

  • Effectively work cross-functionally across the organization to shape Harvey’s solutions to meet customer needs. Collaborate closely with the engineering and product teams to stay updated on the latest AI advancements and tailor solutions to meet client goals.

  • Travel is occasionally required to meet with customers, approximately 1–3 times per quarter.

What You Have

  • Proven track record of selling complex software solutions, with the ability to successfully execute on a consultative, solutions-oriented, value-based selling methodology.

  • Excited about prospecting, and capable of independently leading a sales cycle from start to finish

  • Ability to independently manage a pipeline, accurately forecast key sales performance metrics, and consistently maintain CRM hygiene

  • Ability to lead a complex, multi-threaded sale with stakeholders ranging from executives across various functions to day-to-day product users – especially the ability to convey technical concepts to non-technical audiences.

  • Demonstrated passion for Harvey’s mission and strong understanding of AI and its potential applications in knowledge work. Interest in the legal profession and helping lawyers do their jobs better and more efficiently.

  • Team player who can collaborate effectively across internal functions (product, legal, etc.) to achieve common goals.

  • Energized by contributing to the development of our team, sales processes, and culture, refining the value proposition of our solutions and creating sales resources to drive our success.

  • Experience working in or adjacent to the Legal industry a plus but not required

Compensation

$240,000 OTE with a 50/50 split

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey is building AI-native software for professional services. Our customers trust us with highly sensitive information and critical business workflows, making security fundamental to everything we build. We’re looking for a Director of Detection and Response to build and lead the team that identifies threats, responds decisively to incidents, and turns what we learn into stronger defenses.

You will own Harvey’s Detection and Response strategy, technical direction, and operational readiness across our production platform and corporate environment. Working with the CISO and leaders across Engineering, Infrastructure, IT, Legal, and Customer Trust, you’ll translate business risk into a focused program that protects customer data and enables Harvey to move quickly with confidence.

This is a technical leadership role for someone who can build an exceptional team, earn the trust of senior engineers, and bring clarity to high-stakes situations. You’ll develop a function that scales through software, automation, and strong partnerships, while staying close enough to the work to challenge detection designs and guide complex investigations.

What You'll Do

  • Build and lead the organization. Hire and develop detection engineers, incident responders, and technical leaders; establish clear ownership and a culture of curiosity, sound judgment, and continuous learning. Own the roadmap, staffing plan, and investment decisions.

  • Own incident response and crisis readiness. Lead Harvey’s response to major security incidents, coordinating investigation, containment, recovery, and executive communication. Build clear severity criteria, escalation paths, playbooks, and sustainable 24/7 coverage for critical threats; develop incident commanders and cross-functional responders through exercises.

  • Build detection as an engineering capability. Set the technical direction for telemetry, detection pipelines, forensic tooling, and response automation across cloud, endpoint, identity, SaaS, and application environments. Apply software engineering practices to test detections, improve signal quality, and reduce manual work; evaluate AI-assisted investigation with measurable quality and appropriate human oversight.

  • Focus defenses on meaningful threats. Use threat intelligence, hunting, and an attacker’s perspective to prioritize scenarios that matter to Harvey, including account compromise, data theft, insider risk, privileged-access abuse, and abuse of AI-enabled workflows. Partner with offensive security and platform owners to validate coverage and close blind spots.

  • Make response a company capability. Partner with Engineering, IT, Legal, Privacy, Communications, and Customer Trust on sensitive investigations and crisis decisions. Establish clear escalation and decision authority, preserve evidence, and provide accurate findings to support Legal-led notification and disclosure decisions. Prepare cross-functional responders to contribute when incidents require broader support.

  • Turn incidents into lasting improvements. Drive blameless reviews and ensure corrective actions have owners, deadlines, and verified outcomes. Measure detection coverage, time to detect and contain, recurring failure modes, and responder workload, and use those results to guide investments and reduce customer impact.

What You Have

  • Experience building and leading Detection and Response, incident response, or security engineering teams in a technology company with complex production systems. A record of hiring strong engineers, developing technical leaders, and scaling both the team and its operating model.

  • Deep incident response experience and demonstrated judgment during serious security events. You can lead investigations with incomplete information, make timely containment decisions, and communicate clearly with executives, engineers, and business partners. You bring composure, integrity, and discretion to sensitive investigations and decisions under scrutiny.

  • Strong technical foundations in cloud infrastructure, operating systems, networking, identity, and attacker tradecraft, with depth in detection engineering, threat hunting, or digital forensics. You understand how to investigate across corporate and production environments.

  • An engineering approach to security operations, backed by experience building detection platforms, investigation tools, or response automation. You can evaluate architecture and code, guide senior engineers, and make practical decisions about what to build, buy, or retire.

  • The ability to turn business risk into a focused strategy and deliver it through influence and partnership. You balance urgent response with long-term engineering work and build a demanding, supportive environment where people can do their best work.

Experience protecting enterprise SaaS, sensitive customer data, or AI/ML environments is especially valuable, as is experience investigating insider threats, partnering on privileged-access governance, or leading response under regulatory and public scrutiny.

At Harvey, you’ll shape how an AI company detects and responds to threats as its products and customers evolve. Your team’s work will directly protect customer trust and help make security a durable foundation for the business.

Compensation

$280,000 - $385,000 USD

We’re looking for a Director of Detection and Response to build and lead the team that identifies threats, responds decisively to incidents, and turns what we learn into stronger defenses.



You will own Harvey’s Detection and Response strategy, technical direction, and operational readiness across our production platform and corporate environment. Working with the CISO and leaders across Engineering, Infrastructure, IT, Legal, and Customer Trust, you’ll translate business risk into a focused program that protects customer data and enables Harvey to move quickly with confidence.



This is a technical leadership role for someone who can build an exceptional team, earn the trust of senior engineers, and bring clarity to high-stakes situations. You’ll develop a function that scales through software, automation, and strong partnerships, while staying close enough to the work to challenge detection designs and guide complex investigations.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and lead the organization. Hire and develop detection engineers, incident responders, and technical leaders; establish clear ownership and a culture of curiosity, sound judgment, and continuous learning. Own the roadmap, staffing plan, and investment decisions.

 - Own incident response and crisis readiness. Lead Harvey’s response to major security incidents, coordinating investigation, containment, recovery, and executive communication. Build clear severity criteria, escalation paths, playbooks, and sustainable 24/7 coverage for critical threats; develop incident commanders and cross-functional responders through exercises.

 - Build detection as an engineering capability. Set the technical direction for telemetry, detection pipelines, forensic tooling, and response automation across cloud, endpoint, identity, SaaS, and application environments. Apply software engineering practices to test detections, improve signal quality, and reduce manual work; evaluate AI-assisted investigation with measurable quality and appropriate human oversight.

 - Focus defenses on meaningful threats. Use threat intelligence, hunting, and an attacker’s perspective to prioritize scenarios that matter to Harvey, including account compromise, data theft, insider risk, privileged-access abuse, and abuse of AI-enabled workflows. Partner with offensive security and platform owners to validate coverage and close blind spots.

 - Make response a company capability. Partner with Engineering, IT, Legal, Privacy, Communications, and Customer Trust on sensitive investigations and crisis decisions. Establish clear escalation and decision authority, preserve evidence, and provide accurate findings to support Legal-led notification and disclosure decisions. Prepare cross-functional responders to contribute when incidents require broader support.

 - Turn incidents into lasting improvements. Drive blameless reviews and ensure corrective actions have owners, deadlines, and verified outcomes. Measure detection coverage, time to detect and contain, recurring failure modes, and responder workload, and use those results to guide investments and reduce customer impact.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Experience building and leading Detection and Response, incident response, or security engineering teams in a technology company with complex production systems. A record of hiring strong engineers, developing technical leaders, and scaling both the team and its operating model.

 - Deep incident response experience and demonstrated judgment during serious security events. You can lead investigations with incomplete information, make timely containment decisions, and communicate clearly with executives, engineers, and business partners. You bring composure, integrity, and discretion to sensitive investigations and decisions under scrutiny.

 - Strong technical foundations in cloud infrastructure, operating systems, networking, identity, and attacker tradecraft, with depth in detection engineering, threat hunting, or digital forensics. You understand how to investigate across corporate and production environments.

 - An engineering approach to security operations, backed by experience building detection platforms, investigation tools, or response automation. You can evaluate architecture and code, guide senior engineers, and make practical decisions about what to build, buy, or retire.

 - The ability to turn business risk into a focused strategy and deliver it through influence and partnership. You balance urgent response with long-term engineering work and build a demanding, supportive environment where people can do their best work.



Experience protecting enterprise SaaS, sensitive customer data, or AI/ML environments is especially valuable, as is experience investigating insider threats, partnering on privileged-access governance, or leading response under regulatory and public scrutiny.



At Harvey, you’ll shape how an AI company detects and responds to threats as its products and customers evolve. Your team’s work will directly protect customer trust and help make security a durable foundation for the business.




COMPENSATION

$280,000 - $385,000 USD
